articles.title: Modi expected to meet Trump on the sidelines of the G7 summit in France - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to meet President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the G7 summit in Evian, France. The meeting will be their first since February 2025 and is anticipated to cover bilateral trade negotiations and other regional and global concerns.  The details of the planned discussion were not elaborated upon by officials who confirmed the meeting.

articles.title: TVK government comes under fire for blocking channels on Arasu Cable TV - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, general secretary of the AIADMK, complained that telecasts from three Tamil television channels, Polimer News, News Tamil TV 24X7, and Tamil Janam News, were blocked on the platform of Arasu Cable TV. He cited a similar incident involving Puthiya Thalaimurai a few weeks prior, where protests by the Opposition led to its reinstatement. Palaniswami questioned whether there was an oversight body monitoring electronic media and social media content.

articles.title: BJP councillor arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Sugathan, a BJP councillor, was arrested by the Vattiyurkavu police on Tuesday night after evading arrest for over a month in connection with a clash at the Vellaikkadavu temple.  The arrest led to tension as some BJP workers attempted to block the police from taking him into custody.

articles.title: Chief negotiator Darpan Jain briefs Bengaluru’s IT firms, GCCs, MSMEs on FTA opportunities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Darpan Jain, Additional Secretary in the Department of Commerce, met with large domestic tech firms, Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and MSMEs in Bengaluru on Tuesday. The purpose of these meetings was to educate businesses about the provisions of India's nine FTAs concluded over the past five years, aiming to clarify the export and import scope of these agreements for better understanding.

articles.title: CREDAI supports Parandur project, says second airport for Chennai is necessary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CREDAI has urged the government to prioritize a second airport for Chennai, arguing that current infrastructure limitations are hindering growth and attracting new airlines.  The organization cites data indicating the existing airport could reach saturation by 2028-2032, prompting concerns about lost investment opportunities. P. Kruthivas, president-elect of CREDAI Chennai and managing director of Pushkar Properties Private Limited, emphasizes the strategic benefits of the Parandur project, highlighting its proximity to key industrial zones and infrastructure.

articles.title: BMC vigilance department flagged structural faults in Mrinaltai Gore flyover 5 years before it was inaugurated | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Pratip Acharya, a seasoned journalist based in Mumbai, has spent over a decade reporting for The Indian Express.  His expertise lies in urban governance and civic affairs, covering topics such as city planning, local infrastructure, and political dynamics. He has extensive experience in high-stakes elections, including the Lok Sabha elections of 2014 and 2019, and the Maharashtra Assembly elections of 2019. Acharya's commitment to reporting during the Covid-19 pandemic further highlights his trustworthiness as a source for news from India's critical metropolitan centres.

articles.title: Chola and Hoysala idols at risk during Egmore Museum renovation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Renovation work at the Egmore Government Museum in Tamil Nadu is causing concern as ancient idols and sculptures seized by the Idol Wing of the police are being stored haphazardly, exposed to the elements.  The renovation project, which involves painting the Geology Wing built in 1851, has placed these priceless artifacts at risk, with some even resting on top of construction equipment.  Visitors and workers have expressed dismay over the lack of proper protection for these historical treasures, many dating back centuries and potentially worth millions. This issue has been raised by activists and historians who call for improved facilities and a dedicated effort to safeguard the museum's collection.

articles.title: Mumbai water tanker strike called off after CM Fadnavis intervenes, operators assured notices will be revoked | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Mumbai Water Tankers Association called off its strike after Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis intervened and directed the collectors to withdraw notices issued to tanker operators. The strike, which began on Monday after the state government's district Tehsildar office asked owners and operators of ring-wells and borewells to stop supplying water to tankers, had left residents struggling with a severe water crisis.  The association argued that the new CGWA guidelines were expensive for Mumbai residents, while some residents reported increased water cuts and extended timings.

articles.title: "Must Respond": Trump Says US Apache Helicopter Was Shot Down By Iran
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump confirmed that a US Army Apache helicopter was shot down by Iran near the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The two pilots were rescued after spending two hours in the water and are unharmed.  Trump stated that the US "must" respond to the attack, but previously expressed optimism about negotiating a deal with Iran.  Mediators, led by Pakistan, have been trying for weeks to reach an agreement between the two countries.

articles.title: Zojila tunnel is a gamechanger for national security, integration: Nitin Gadkari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitin Gadkari, Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways, oversaw the breakthrough of the 13.14 km long Zojila tunnel, calling it a "gamechanger" for national security and integration. The tunnel, Asia's longest single-tube bi-directional road tunnel at an altitude of 11,578 ft, was completed at a cost of ₹6,800 crore despite an initial estimate of ₹12,000 crore.  Omar Abdullah, J&K Chief Minister, and Manoj Sinha, J&K Lieutenant Governor, also attended the ceremony expressing their support for the project's benefits to the region.

articles.title: 'This Is Our Finest Hour': Israeli Ambassador Reuven Azar Celebrates Deepening Ties With India
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's ambassador to India, Reuven Azar, addressed a reception in New Delhi on Tuesday evening, emphasizing the resilience of Israel despite ongoing conflict. He highlighted the country's economic success and its strategic partnership with India, citing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit earlier this year as a key development.  Azar emphasized that both nations share common values, including vitality and entrepreneurship, and that defense cooperation between them is expanding. The ambassador concluded by offering a prayer for peace in the region and around the world.

articles.title: Farmer harnesses wife to plough after ox dies, Rohit Pawar seeks help | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rohit Pawar, NCP (SP) MLA, has raised concerns about the plight of a farmer in Latur district who was forced to harness his wife to a plow after one of his oxen died from lightning strike.  The farmer, Kashinath Gaikwad, lacks financial resources to purchase another ox and is facing hardship due to this situation. Pawar called for immediate assistance for the family and urged authorities to consider a blanket loan waiver for farmers.

articles.title: Dua Lipa flaunts Rs 2 crore watch at her Sicily wedding welcome party | Fashion News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner kicked off their Italian wedding celebrations in Palermo, Sicily with a welcome party that caused local outrage over the city's shutdown.  The couple compensated affected residents financially to reach a truce. Lipa wore a custom-made Bottega Veneta dress for the dinner, paired with Bulgari jewelry including a Serpenti necklace and Pallini watch. The Pallini bracelet watch features thousands of tiny yellow-gold beads interspersed with diamonds, and is an iconic piece from the 1950s and 60s.  The Tubogas Manchette cuff watch, inspired by a 1948 design, was also worn by Lipa and retails for EUR 194,000.

articles.title: Woman, 55, Mauled To Death By Leopard In Uttarakhand, Wild Cat Shot Dead
articles.rephrased_article: A 55-year-old woman, identified as Prabha Devi, was killed by a leopard in Pauri Garhwal district's Badi village.  Forest department officials responded to the incident and found her body near an abandoned structure. The leopard, which was present near the body, charged at the search party and was subsequently shot dead. A post-mortem examination will be conducted on the leopard's carcass.

articles.title: ₹95,962 crore set aside for VB-G RAM G - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Rural Development Minister, announced an interim allocation of ₹95,692.31 crore for the new rural employment scheme, Vikshit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-GRAM G). This sum does not include the State governments’ share, which will vary depending on their contribution. The combined outlay for the scheme is expected to reach ₹1.25 lakh crore.  While 26 States have completed the necessary procedural requirements, four states — Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana, and Mizoram — are yet to finalize all formalities. Despite a change in government in West Bengal, the issue of settling pending dues under MGNREGS remains unresolved.

articles.title: PoK Protests Joint Awami Action Committee 1 Crore Bounty, Arrest Warrants: PoK's Hunt For 4 Protest Leaders
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan-occupied Kashmir administration has announced a reward of 1 crore Pakistani rupees for information leading to the arrest of four leaders of the banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The JAAC, which was protesting assembly seat reservations and other issues, has been accused by authorities of inciting violence and is now designated as a "terror" organization.  The crackdown on protesters in PoK has resulted in over 100 deaths and hundreds of arrests. India condemned the actions and called for international accountability. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) also expressed concern about the use of excessive force and the suppression of dissent.

articles.title: Today Weather LIVE, Heatwave Today, Rain Alert Highlights: Delhi-NCR To Witness More Rain, Says Weather Office
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast light rainfall and thunderstorms with gusty winds of up to 60 kmph for Delhi and neighboring regions on June 11 and 12.  This weather change is expected to bring a drop in temperatures, offering relief from the heatwave conditions that have persisted across the region. Meanwhile, attention is shifting to the progress of the southwest monsoon, which entered Kerala on June 4. The IMD reports favorable conditions for its gradual advancement across southern and central parts of the country.  The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has activated a technology-driven preparedness plan across key Metro lines ahead of the monsoon season.

articles.title: Indian-American CEO Facing US Citizenship Loss Over H-1B Visa Fraud
articles.rephrased_article: Neeraj Sharma, a 50-year-old Indian-American businessman, is among 17 individuals facing possible loss of US citizenship due to fraud allegations. Sharma, who was the CEO of New Jersey-based staffing firm Magnavision LLC, allegedly submitted 11 fake H-1B visa applications with forged signatures and provided false information during his naturalization process in 2017. The Justice Department is seeking to revoke his citizenship after he was convicted in a visa fraud case linked to activities between 2015 and 2017. This action marks part of a broader effort by the US government targeting naturalized citizens accused of serious misconduct, with officials describing it as one of the largest denaturalization efforts in US history.

articles.title: Trinamool Congress Crisis, Trinamool: "She Said Will Fight, Rebuild": Kirti Azad On Mamata Banerjee's Crisis Plan
articles.rephrased_article: Kirti Azad, a Trinamool Congress MP, criticized rebel MPs who he called "traitors" and accused them of seeking power. He alleged that these individuals were being blackmailed and threatened with coercion to join the BJP. Mamata Banerjee, the party's chief, has vowed to rebuild the party and fight again on the streets. Azad also claimed that several rebels, including Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, had been caught taking bribes and that they lacked loyalty to the party. He asserted that these individuals would not be able to win in future elections.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of blackmail and coercion within a political party raise serious concerns.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Does referee case show Fifa has lost control of its tournament? - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Fifa's referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the United States for the 2026 World Cup after an 11-hour immigration interview. Fifa maintains it is not involved in host country immigration processes, but the incident raises questions about how the organization allowed this situation to occur. Concerns remain over US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) presence at stadiums and potential impact on fans' access.  The US government has implemented a strict visa policy that has excluded several national teams and supporters from entering the country.

articles.title: Will Hobnobbing With Trinamool Rebels Cost BJP? What State Leaders Say
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the West Bengal Chief Minister, met with rebel Trinamool Congress MPs at Satabdi Roy's Delhi residence. This meeting followed a similar gathering of the rebels at Bhupendra Yadav's home earlier in the day. Despite these meetings, the BJP maintains it will not induct any Trinamool leaders into its ranks. The BJP leadership argues that this gesture is a political move to weaken the Trinamool party and prepare for upcoming elections.  The BJP has stated that they are focused on cleaning Bengal of the Trinamool party.

articles.title: ‘Anything but normal’: Uncertainty as Iranians try to get by amid US war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iranians are grappling with the ongoing war and US sanctions, leading to heightened economic uncertainty.  The recent Israeli-Iranian missile exchanges have further exacerbated the situation, causing daily life disruptions and impacting livelihoods. President Donald Trump's pronouncements on potential peace deals have offered little comfort, as many Iranians struggle to maintain their standard of living amidst soaring inflation and food shortages. Despite some internet access being restored after a prolonged shutdown, concerns remain about government control over information flow.

articles.title: Serena Williams wins on return at Queen's after nearly four years away from tennis - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Serena Williams returned to the court after 1,375 days away from professional tennis, partnering with Canadian teenager Victoria Mboko in a doubles match at Queen's Club. The pair defeated third seeds Erin Routliffe and Nicole Melichar-Martinez, winning 7-6 (7-2) 6-2.  Williams expressed her enjoyment of the experience and acknowledged that she was motivated by seeing her daughters, Olympia and Adira, enjoy the match. She plans to continue playing doubles at Queen's Club later this week.

articles.title: Israel preventing more than 16,500 Palestinians from accessing medical treatment | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has been accused of preventing more than 16,500 Palestinians from accessing medical treatment abroad despite a ceasefire since October 2023. Gaza’s Health Ministry claims that Israel is killing patients with delays and hindering the rebuilding of its healthcare system, which has been systematically destroyed by Israel. The UN Secretary-General, Antonio Guterres, called for the immediate reopening of all crossings into Gaza to allow humanitarian aid to enter without restriction.  The UN and European Union have warned that human development in Gaza has been set back by 77 years due to the ongoing conflict.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Systematic denial of medical care constitutes large-scale harm to citizens.

articles.title: Claude Mythos: Anthropic releases version of AI tool despite risk concerns
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, the company behind the AI tool Claude, has released a version called Claude Fable 5 to the public despite concerns about its potential risks.  The release comes after initial testing of the tool, known as Mythos, raised worries among technology and government leaders about its capabilities. François-Philippe Champagne, Canadian Finance Minister, previously expressed concern over the potential dangers of Mythos. Despite ongoing legal disputes with the US Department of Defense, Anthropic has expanded access to Claude Fable 5 to a limited group of organizations, including cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers. The company aims to expand public access in the future.

articles.title: NASA announces astronauts for Artemis III spaceflight, scheduled for 2027 | Space News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: NASA announced the crew for its Artemis III spaceflight, scheduled to launch in 2027. The four-man crew includes astronauts Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio, Luca Parmitano, and Randy Bresnik, with veteran test pilot Bob Heintz as a backup.  The mission will focus on practicing in-space docking procedures and collecting research data. Concerns remain about the recent explosion of the Blue Origin New Glenn rocket, but NASA officials say they are working with their partners to ensure the Artemis III launch is successful. The Artemis III flight will be a public-private partnership involving three rockets from NASA, Blue Origin, and SpaceX.

articles.title: World Cup referee barred: Somali's Omar Artan had 'right papers and right visa' - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: A Somali referee, Omar Artan, was denied entry to the United States for the World Cup despite holding valid papers and a diplomatic passport. Artans 11-hour immigration interview resulted in his deportation back to Turkey after he was barred from entering the country at Miami International Airport.  The White House Task Force on the World Cup supported the decision by US Customs and Border Patrol, while Fifa confirmed that Artan will not be able to officiate at the tournament.

articles.title: Artemis III: Nasa names astronauts to prepare for Moon landing
articles.rephrased_article: NASA has named its crew for the Artemis III mission, a lunar technology test that will see astronauts orbit Earth and dock with prototype lunar landers.  The mission's commander is Randy Bresnik, pilot is Luca Parmitano, and the mission specialists are Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio. The mission was originally planned as a crewed lunar landing but has been modified due to delays in SpaceX's Starship rocket, which was intended for transporting astronauts from lunar orbit to the surface.  The timeline for Artemis III is now uncertain, with potential setbacks including a recent explosion of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket and challenges with refuelling technology for Starship.

articles.title: 5 lesser-known monsoon treks in India | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Several lesser-known trekking trails in India are offering a quieter, more immersive experience during the monsoon season. The Kudremukh Trek in the Western Ghats is known for its lush green landscapes and rain-fed waterfalls, while Dzukou Valley in Northeast India comes alive with blooming wildflowers and mist.  Chembra Peak in Kerala's Wayanad district offers scenic views of tea plantations and forests transformed by monsoon rains. The Rajmachi Fort Trek, located near Lonavala, combines history with the beauty of monsoon-soaked trails and waterfalls. Finally, Sandakphu, along the India-Nepal border, provides a stunning Himalayan trekking experience with foggy forests and blooming flowers.

articles.title: India pushes for dialogue on climate finance, adaptation at Bonn climate talks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India called for the expansion of adaptation finance and a dedicated agenda space for developed countries to fulfill their obligations under the Paris Agreement at the ongoing UN climate negotiations in Bonn, Germany. The country emphasized that equity and historical responsibility should guide the implementation phase, urging for operationalization of the Just Transition Mechanism based on CBDR-RC principles. India also urged against unilateral trade measures like carbon border levies and stressed the need to preserve the facilitative, non-prescriptive nature of the Mitigation Work Programme.

articles.title: Bowen: Trump and Netanyahu wanted to reshape the Middle East - now they risk a permacrisis
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu believed they could reshape the Middle East after their military action against Iran. However, the Iranian regime has proven more resilient than anticipated, leading to a protracted conflict with no clear end in sight. The downing of an American helicopter by Iran highlights the ongoing risks of escalating tensions.  The US and Israel are now facing a difficult situation as they grapple with how to respond to Iran's actions while also trying to maintain diplomatic efforts.

articles.title: What will the fallout be from the unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir? | India-Pakistan Tensions News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan, the presenter, hosted a discussion on the unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir following clashes between protesters and police that resulted in at least 11 deaths. The Joint Awami Action Committee is protesting a rule granting legislative seats to refugees from India-administered Kashmir, claiming it gives them disproportionate influence.  The government maintains any change would require constitutional reform, highlighting the long-standing political debate over this issue.

articles.title: ‘Singappen’: Vijay launches specialised force for women’s safety with Rs 354-crore allocation, drone surveillance | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: C Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, launched a specialized women's safety force called the Singappen Special Force. The force, backed by over Rs 354 crore, aims to prevent crimes against women and girls through preventive policing, rapid response, and field surveillance. Vijay emphasized that the force is part of a broader law-and-order push, including plans for additional anti-narcotics stations and an aggressive campaign against drug trafficking networks. The launch signifies Vijay's commitment to improving women's safety and ensuring their dignity in the state.

articles.title: Pune RTO strike: Services hit as staff protest stalled restructuring | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Pune’s Regional Transport Office (RTO) clerical staff went on strike on Tuesday, halting vehicle registration transfers, transport permits, duplicate RC issuance, and hypothecation cancellation. The strike stemmed from a four-year delay in implementing a revised recruitment policy for the RTO's clerical department, which resulted in promotions being temporary and subsequently reversed.  The union demands an extension for the 56 promoted officials and compensation for financial losses caused by their demotion. They also want the time-bound promotion policy implemented without further delay to ensure eligible employees receive pay hikes and career advancement.

articles.title: How China built the world's first wind-powered underwater data centre off Shanghai
articles.rephrased_article: China has launched the world's first wind-powered underwater data center in Shanghai, a collaboration between Shanghai Hailanyun Technology and government agencies. The facility uses seawater as a cooling medium to reduce energy consumption and land requirements, achieving a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) below 1.15. This project, which draws electricity from offshore wind power, aims to provide sustainable solutions for data center needs while addressing the growing demand for AI computing in China.  The facility is expected to play a role in shaping the future of sustainable digital infrastructure globally.

articles.title: Arunachal village sees violence over dam: Multiple houses vandalised, prohibitory orders issued | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sukrita Baruah, a Principal Correspondent for The Indian Express, based in Guwahati, provides comprehensive coverage of India's North East region. Her expertise spans ethnic and social dynamics, border and geopolitical issues, governance and policy, including reporting on state elections, tribal council decisions, and central scheme implementation.  Her background as an Education Correspondent in Delhi has equipped her with a sharp analytical lens for policy analysis, student affairs, and educational reforms.

articles.title: We-Vibe Discount Codes and Deals: Up to 60% Off | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: We-Vibe, a company known for its couples sex toys, has expanded its product line to include individual vibrators and massagers. The company's products are designed for both in-person and long-distance sexual pleasure, with features like Bluetooth connectivity and remote control. We-Vibe offers various discounts and promotions, including free gifts with purchases over $199, a 15% discount through email sign-up, and a student discount of 20%.  The company also provides key worker deals for those in the military, healthcare, education, and first responder fields.

articles.title: Trump says Iran downed Apache helicopter, ‘US must respond to attack’ | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that an American Apache helicopter was shot down by Iran while patrolling the Strait of Hormuz, prompting a threat of retaliation. The US Central Command confirmed two crew members were rescued and are in stable condition after their helicopter went down near Oman.  The incident reportedly marks America's first loss of an Apache helicopter since the war with Iran began in February.

articles.title: Soil at Shiv Shakti Point chemically close to lunar meteorite that hit Antarctica | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Chandrayaan-3, India's moon mission, has discovered a close chemical relationship between the soil at its landing site near the Moon's South Pole and a lunar meteorite found in Antarctica.  The study, led by researchers from the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), suggests that the soil at Shiv Shakti Point is similar to the ALHA 81005 meteorite, which fell on Earth about a million years ago. The findings support the theory of a lunar magma ocean and provide evidence for the redistribution of crustal materials by impact events. This information could be valuable for future rover missions aiming to uncover insights into the Moon's early history.

articles.title: Anthropic Offers Mythos Upgrade for Cyber Partners and a ‘Safe’ Version for the Rest of You | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic released two new AI models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5.  The company says these models have greater capabilities than the Mythos Preview model it released in April to a limited set of tech industry partners. Anthropic is currently only releasing Claude Mythos 5 to a limited set of industry partners, many of which received access to Mythos Preview, and the company is collaborating with the US government on the rollout.  Claude Fable 5, which is being publicly released, will have guardrails in place that block certain user requests related to cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry. The company says it hopes to make its classifiers more precise over time but for now, the protective mechanism is built to err on the side of caution.

articles.title: What happens to the body when you ear food wrapped in newspaper?
articles.sentiment_target: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
articles.rephrased_article: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has reiterated its ban on using newspapers for food packaging, citing health risks from newspaper ink containing heavy metals and disease-causing microbes.  Dr Disha Bhatia, a Consultant and Hospital Infection Control Officer, Microbiology at Aakash Healthcare, warns that the chemicals in printing inks can leach into food when hot or greasy, posing serious health risks including cognitive impairment and cancer. The FSSAI has directed all food businesses to use approved food-grade packaging materials instead.

articles.title: Air India Passenger Breaks Window Pane Mid-Flight, No-Fly Action Looms
articles.rephrased_article: An Air India passenger on flight AI1879 from Chandigarh to Delhi damaged the inner window pane of the aircraft during landing. The incident occurred after the passenger ignored repeated warnings from cabin crew, prompting the cockpit crew to alert security agencies and follow standard operating procedures.  The airline has referred the matter to its internal committee for further review, which will determine whether the passenger should be classified as unruly and placed on a no-fly list.

articles.title: NASA unveils Artemis III astronauts to test technology for future moon landing | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: NASA announced the crew for its Artemis III mission, which will focus on testing the Orion capsule's docking with lunar landers. The crew consists of Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, Andre Douglas, and Luca Parmitano.  The two-week demonstration is scheduled for 2027 and aims to prepare for a lunar landing in 2028.  SpaceX and Blue Origin are competing to deliver the landers, with Blue Origin recently experiencing a setback during an engine test.

articles.title: The Top New Features in Apple’s iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple's WWDC 2026 keynote focused on stability improvements and enhanced usability in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.  The updates include Siri upgrades, faster app launches, improved photo processing, and new parental controls. Siri is now a more capable assistant with an updated look and features like natural voice interaction and visual search integration. Apple Intelligence is available on select iPhones, including the iPhone 15 Pro and newer, while older devices will receive limited benefits.  The Photos app introduces AI-powered tools such as "Extend" for image editing and "Spatial Reframing" for perspective alteration. Safari features improved tab organization, notification alerts, and custom extensions. The Messages and Mail apps now offer one-tap actions for reminders and event creation. Apple also announced updates to the Health app, Home app, iCloud Shared Albums, and Passwords app, among other improvements.

articles.title: Terror Hideout To Purple Revolution: How Lavender Changed Fate Of A Bhaderwah in Jammu and Kashmir
articles.rephrased_article: Bhadarwah, a town in Jammu and Kashmir's Doda district, is transforming from a former terror hideout into a lavender farming hub.  The cultivation of lavender has provided farmers with new income sources and attracted domestic and international buyers, boosting tourism in the region. Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted this initiative during his "Mann Ki Baat" program, recognizing the success of the lavender revolution in Bhaderwah. The initiative has also been praised by Dr Jitendra Singh, who noted that it provided a new economic opportunity for the region and proved that entrepreneurship doesn't require advanced degrees.

articles.title: Serena Williams returns to professional tennis at Queen's Club
articles.rephrased_article: Serena Williams returned to professional tennis on Tuesday, partnering with 19-year-old Victoria Mboko in a doubles match at Queen's Club. This marked her first professional match since 2022 and she received a standing ovation from the crowd.  Williams also announced she will compete in the Berlin Open in doubles before deciding whether to play singles at Wimbledon, which starts June 29th.

articles.title: Trump booed ‘thunderously’ at NBA Finals: What we know | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was booed by fans at Madison Square Garden during the NBA Finals, despite being the first sitting president to attend. Adam Silver, NBA commissioner, stated that the president is a "genuine Knicks fan" and emphasized the unifying nature of sports. Security measures were heightened for Trump's visit, including checkpoints, police presence, and counter-drone technology. While some New Yorkers criticized Trump's presence as disruptive, others appreciated his attempt to connect with fans.

articles.title: 8 Burnt Alive In Fire At Illegal Cracker Godown In Jaipur
articles.rephrased_article: Eight individuals were killed in a fire that erupted at an illegal cracker godown in Khoh Nagoriyan area. The fire, which started after an explosion, engulfed the small house where combustible materials were stored. Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, Congress leader Ashok Gehlot, and Jaipur Collector Sandesh Nayak offered condolences to the victims' families.  Police Commissioner Sachin Mittal stated that the house was being used as a storage facility for firecrackers, while MLA Amin Kagzi accused authorities of negligence in allowing such a hazardous facility to operate near residential areas.

articles.title: Mohali Man Kills Ex-Lover, Slits Own Throat, Reaches Court Days Later
articles.rephrased_article: Harjinder Singh Mann, who killed his ex-partner Dimple inside a logistics firm in Mohali on June 4th, appeared at court walking unaided despite extensive throat injuries he sustained from self-inflicted wounds.  The incident occurred after Dimple ended their relationship and refused to discuss their past, leading to persistent harassment. Mann was accused of stabbing Dimple multiple times before turning the knife on himself.  Police are investigating the case and gathering statements from witnesses.

articles.title: Italy’s foreign minister slams Israel’s Ben-Gvir over ‘flip-flop’ comments | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Antonio Tajani, Italy’s Foreign Minister, condemned Itamar Ben-Gvir, the Israeli National Security Minister, for his "unacceptable" comments regarding Italy's investigation into the treatment of activists detained by Israel.  Ben-Gvir had previously criticized Italy's geographical shape and sparked international outrage after a video surfaced showing him mocking and mistreating activists in Ashdod port. The EU is considering sanctions against Ben-Gvir, while Italy has suspended its defense agreement with Israel and remains one of the strongest allies of Israel in Europe despite growing tensions.

articles.title: MacOS 27 Golden Gate: Top New Features | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple unveiled macOS 27 Golden Gate, a new operating system designed to integrate advanced AI features. The update is exclusive to Apple Silicon Macs and includes a redesigned Siri chatbot powered by Google Gemini, offering natural language processing and image generation capabilities.  The new version of Siri will be available in July as part of the public beta program. Other notable updates include improvements to Safari with tab organization, Shortcuts app automation, and Image Playground's enhanced image generation features.

articles.title: 'Not Done By Us': Surat Civic Body Distances Itself From Nasirnagar Demolition
articles.rephrased_article: The Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) has denied any involvement in the demolition of homes in Nasirnagar, Surat.  Ashish J Nayak, Deputy Commissioner of the SMC, stated that his team was only there for boundary demarcation and that machinery was already operating when they arrived. He also clarified that the police and SOG were not summoned by the SMC and that the standard procedure for demolition notices is followed, which includes providing residents with advance notice. The state government is investigating the incident to determine who authorized the demolition.

articles.title: Indian-Origin Couple Aditi Paralkar Rakesh Pai, 9-Year-Old Son Jump To Death From 36th Floor Of London Flat
articles.rephrased_article: Rakesh Pai, Aditi Paralkar, and their nine-year-old son, Sid, died after falling from the balcony of their 36th-floor London apartment on May 27.  Police are investigating the incident as an "unexpected" death, with local MP Neil Coyle suggesting the child's serious health conditions may have contributed to the family's decision. Julian Morris, senior coroner for the London inner south area, has referred the case to his office and is awaiting the official causes of death during an inquest.

articles.title: Jio BlackRock prepares ETF debut by August after building $2 billion India fund base - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jio BlackRock Asset Management, a joint venture between Mukesh Ambani's Jio Financial Services and the world's largest asset manager, BlackRock, has amassed $1.9 billion in assets under management within a year of launch. The company plans to start with equity-focused ETF strategies, aiming to tap into India's growing retail investor interest in ETFs.  Jio BlackRock believes tighter bid-offer spreads and innovative strategies can improve liquidity and boost participation in the Indian ETF market.

articles.title: Congress, Trinamool Congress: After Hug At INDIA Huddle, A Mamata Banerjee-Sonia Gandhi Meet At 10 Janpath
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, leader of the Trinamool Congress, met with Sonia Gandhi, chairperson of the Congress Parliamentary Party, at her residence in Delhi. The meeting followed a recent photo of their embrace at an INDIA bloc meeting and comes amid significant challenges for both parties, including rebellions within their ranks.  Experts suggest that no major discussions took place without Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, present.

articles.title: Franco-German fighter jet scrapping leaves European allies at odds
articles.rephrased_article: Germany has scrapped its joint fighter jet program with France, citing disagreements between the two nations over control and strategic goals. The project, known as Future Combat Air System (FCAS), was intended to strengthen Franco-German relations but ultimately failed due to differing visions for the aircraft's capabilities and leadership roles within the program.  Germany has indicated that core aspects of the project will continue, though the future remains uncertain. France, however, expressed regret over the decision and emphasized the importance of continued Franco-German cooperation in defense.

articles.title: World Cup opening ceremony: Who’s performing, when it starts, how to watch | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 FIFA World Cup opening ceremonies will take place in Mexico City, Toronto, and Los Angeles.  Each ceremony will feature unique performances by artists like Shakira, Tyla, Alejandro Fernandez, and more. The events are designed to showcase the cultural identity of each host nation while uniting them through football.  The ceremonies will be broadcast worldwide and attended by an estimated 200,000 spectators.  However, protests in Mexico City and security concerns in Los Angeles and Toronto remain potential challenges for the opening ceremonies.

articles.title: Afghanistan: Two dead after women take part in Herat protest
articles.rephrased_article: Taliban police in Herat, Afghanistan, used live fire to disperse a protest against the detention of women accused of violating strict Islamic dress codes. Two people reportedly died and several others were injured during the incident, according to witnesses and medics.  The Herat Police Command denied any deaths but acknowledged they responded to the protest, while Richard Bennett, the United Nations' special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Afghanistan, condemned the excessive use of force against peaceful protesters.

articles.title: Nigeria plays Portugal in international World Cup friendly: All to know | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Portugal will face Nigeria in a World Cup warm-up match on Wednesday. The game, taking place at the Estadio Dr Magalhaes Pessoa in Leiria, Portugal, is part of Portugal's preparations for the 2026 World Cup.  The match follows Portugal's victory over Chile and will be their final warm-up before flying to North America.  Nigeria, who are not participating in the upcoming World Cup, will look to test Portugal's squad ahead of their return to African competition.

articles.title: UzChess Cup 2026: Arjun Erigaisi holds steady for joint lead; Vidit Gujrathi opens account with draw
articles.rephrased_article: Mukhiddin Madaminov, Arjun Erigaisi, and Nodirbek Abdusattorov are tied for first place after the third round of the UzChess Cup 2026 Masters event in Tashkent.  After a second round that saw all five games produce decisive results, the third round brought back normalcy with four draws and one result. Vidit Gujrathi, who had lost his previous two games, finally scored a draw against Abdusattorov. The Indian players will face each other in the fourth round on Wednesday.

articles.title: Murder of Lyhanna, 11, enrages France and turns up heat on government
articles.rephrased_article: France's government is facing intense pressure following the murder of 11-year-old Lyhanna, whose alleged killer had been reported to police multiple times for suspected sexual abuse.  Over 60,000 people protested across the country demanding the resignation of Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin, who has acknowledged "shocking and unacceptable failings" in the state's services but refuses to step down. The suspect, Jérôme Barella, was taken into custody three days after Lyhanna's disappearance, denying any involvement but admitting driving her to a swimming pool.  Rosa's mother is filing a lawsuit against the state and Darmanin for their responsibilities in the affair.

articles.title: Kenya’s police crack down on protest against US Ebola centre in Nanyuki | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kenya's police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse a crowd of protesters who clashed with officers in Nanyuki, where they were demonstrating against a US-run Ebola quarantine center.  The protest stemmed from anger among Kenyans over the relocation of potential Ebola carriers into their country. The proposed center at the Laikipia Air Base was nearing completion despite a temporary halt order from the High Court and opposition from local politicians. President William Ruto's government has pledged to continue with the project, citing past US support for Kenya's Ebola preparedness efforts.

articles.title: Israeli air strikes hit Lebanese city of Tyre despite Iranian warning to stop attacks
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has continued its airstrikes in southern Lebanon despite a warning from Iran to cease attacks. The strikes have resulted in the deaths of at least 13 people, including eight in the city of Tyre, where residents were ordered to evacuate their homes.  The Israeli military claims it is dismantling Hezbollah infrastructure while also reporting the death of a "terrorist" who crossed into Israel from Lebanon. Hezbollah retaliated by firing rockets at several Israeli sites and using drones against troops and vehicles. The conflict has complicated efforts by President Donald Trump to broker a peace deal between the US, Israel, and Iran.

articles.title: Trump says Iran shot down US helicopter over Hormuz, vows to respond | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump accused Iran of shooting down a US military helicopter over the Strait of Hormuz, stating that the United States must respond to the attack.  While both pilots were rescued and are unharmed, Trump vowed retaliation despite the incident occurring after an April 8 truce between the US and Iran paused the US-Israeli war against Iran. The incident comes amidst escalating tensions in the region, including recent attacks on Iranian oil tankers and Israeli strikes inside Iran.  Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has stated that his country is not afraid to return to war, while Sina Azodi, director of the Middle East studies program at Georgetown University, says Iran is attempting to pressure the US to finalize an agreement ending the conflict.

articles.title: Trump says Iran shot down US helicopter and vows to respond
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump accused Iran of shooting down a US helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz, vowing to respond. The incident occurred while two crew members were patrolling regional waters and resulted in the crash of an AH-64 Apache helicopter.  The two pilots were rescued by a drone operated by US 5th Fleet's Task Force 59 within two hours of the crash. Iran's top negotiator, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, responded with a threat to use stronger language if the US did not fulfill its commitments.

articles.title: After Nagorno-Karabakh, Armenians vote for peace over nationalism | Elections | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nikol Pashinyan, the Prime Minister of Armenia, won a second term in office after securing 49.8% of the vote in Sunday's election. The victory suggests a shift away from Russian influence and towards a more peace-oriented future for Armenia.  The loss of Nagorno-Karabakh to Azerbaijan in 2023 has prompted Armenians to prioritize peace over nationalism, with Pashinyan's vision of normalizing relations with Azerbaijan and Turkey gaining traction. While opposition parties, including Strong Armenia and Armenia Alliance, secured a combined 41 seats, their influence is likely limited by internal divisions.  Despite the weakening of Russian influence in Armenia, Moscow still holds significant economic leverage over Yerevan and could pose a challenge to Pashinyan's efforts to normalize relations with Azerbaijan and Turkey.

articles.title: Indian founder Swapnil Srivastav gets rejected for US visa for 'not enough ties to home country' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Indian entrepreneur Swapnil Srivastav, co-founder of a bamboo-based kids' wear brand, was recently denied a US tourist visa despite having a successful business and strong ties to India. Srivastav argued that his company employs over 100 people, receives funding from top investors, and serves millions of Indian families. He plans to reapply for the visa but faces a trend of other Indian entrepreneurs facing similar rejections due to concerns about their ties to India.

articles.title: Alicia Hempleman-Adams becomes first British woman to cross Atlantic in hydrogen balloon | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alicia Hempleman-Adams, a 36-year-old British explorer, successfully completed the first transatlantic journey in a hydrogen gas balloon from Maine to Europe.  She flew alongside fellow balloonists Bert Padelt and Peter Cuneo, facing harsh conditions including freezing temperatures and strong winds during the four-day flight. The team encountered challenges throughout the journey, requiring constant monitoring of weather conditions and adaptation to changing circumstances.  Hempleman-Adams, who holds several aviation records, is now the first British woman to cross the Atlantic in a hydrogen gas balloon, following in her father's footsteps.

articles.title: Scotland changed its buildings forever to save disappearing birds: Tiny 'swift bricks' will now be built into new homes | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scotland has become the first UK nation to mandate bird-friendly nesting spaces in new buildings, known as "swift bricks," through its Natural Environment legislation. These specially designed cavities provide nesting sites for birds like swifts, sparrows, and starlings, addressing a growing concern about declining urban bird populations. The initiative is supported by conservation groups such as the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB), who view it as a simple and cost-effective way to improve biodiversity in future developments. Swift bricks are integrated into building construction during the initial phase, providing permanent nesting spaces that can last for decades with minimal maintenance.

articles.title: Indian students asked 'how do I get a data engineering job in the US': Tech founder says $100K H-1B visa fee made the answer depressing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zach Wilson, a former Meta engineer, expressed pride in being an American after a federal court struck down the $100,000 fee imposed by the Trump administration on H-1B visa holders.  Wilson stated that he had to visit India this year due to the fees and believes the US is losing out on talent by not welcoming foreign workers. He also acknowledged the backlash from some social media users who criticized his stance on training American students, but defended his position by stating he has never faced discrimination under Indian managers.

articles.title: Promoter sells Rs 1,024 crore worth of Ajanta Pharma shares in block deal to Kotak MF and ABSL MF - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ajanta Pharma saw significant share purchases by Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, acquiring 21.02 lakh and 13.48 lakh shares respectively at a price of Rs 2,968 per share. The pharmaceutical company has been performing well in the market due to steady earnings growth, healthy margins, and a robust balance sheet.  Elara Capital raised its FY27E-FY28E core earnings estimates for Ajanta Pharma, citing strong US generics business growth and a positive fourth quarter performance.

articles.title: 6 devotees injured after balcony collapses near Mathura’s Banke Bihari temple | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A dilapidated balcony collapsed on a crowded lane leading to the Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan, injuring at least six devotees. Mathura Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shlok Kumar said monkeys were likely sitting on the balcony when it gave way.  Local authorities are investigating the cause of the collapse and examining nearby old buildings for safety concerns. The incident briefly disrupted temple traffic but was quickly resolved.

articles.title: After Japan, Nepal Bans Import Of Indian Mangoes Over This Issue
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal has banned imports of Indian mangoes due to excessive pesticide levels detected in shipments. The ban, imposed by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development, began around April-May and is expected to disrupt exports during the crucial summer mango season. Local traders warn that domestic supply may not meet demand, potentially leading to shortages.  The government claims the move will promote local fruit production but faces concerns from exporters who fear it could damage India's agricultural quality control systems.

articles.title: Property registration to trigger automatic mutation in Haryana | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Haryana government has implemented an auto-mutation system to streamline land record updates. This new system automatically generates mutation entries during property registration, eliminating the need for separate applications and reducing paperwork.  Financial Commissioner Revenue and Disaster Management Department, Sumita Misra, stated that this reform aims to save time and effort for property owners while improving accuracy and minimizing disputes. The initiative is part of a broader modernization drive to enhance land governance through digital technologies.

articles.title: Fake IDs, Fake Cop Badges, Fake Money: Bengal Killer Couple's 'World Of Fake'
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police recovered fake IDs, police badges, counterfeit currency bundles, and over 100 shirts from the accused couple's home in connection with the murder of Delhi University Assistant Professor Debosmita Paul. The investigation revealed that the couple had planned the attack meticulously, conducting reconnaissance for several days before the murder. They also attempted to conceal their identities after the crime by changing clothes multiple times and taking a circuitous route to avoid suspicion.  The police are now investigating if the accused were involved in any other crimes.

articles.title: PM Modi speaks to Amir of Kuwait, expresses concern over escalation of tensions in West Asia | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Sheikh Meshal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al Sabah, the Amir of Kuwait, on Tuesday to discuss escalating tensions in West Asia.  The conversation came days after an Indian national was killed in an Iranian attack on Kuwait International Airport and followed India's condemnation of the attacks on Kuwait's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Modi reiterated his call for de-escalation, dialogue, and diplomacy to restore peace and stability while thanking the Amir for his concern for the safety of the large Indian community in Kuwait.

articles.title: Rivian R2 2026: Specs, Price, Availability | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Rivian has released its new midsize electric SUV, the R2, aimed at a mass market audience. The R2 starts at $45,000, significantly lower than the company's previous models and rivals like Tesla Model Y. Despite this competitive price point, the R2 is not without limitations. It will initially be equipped with Gen 2 hardware, lacking the advanced features of its upcoming Gen 3 system. The R2 also lacks lidar and a fully functional Level 3 autonomous driving system. However, it boasts impressive performance, off-road capability, and a user-friendly interface, including its innovative "Halo" steering wheel controls.  The company is confident that the R2 will be a significant revenue driver for Rivian, but further testing and refinement are needed to confirm its success.

articles.title: Indian students asked 'how do I get a data engineering job in the US': Tech founder says $100K H-1B visa fee made the answer depressing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zach Wilson, a former Meta engineer, expressed pride in being an American after a federal court struck down the $100,000 fee imposed by the Trump administration on H-1B visa holders.  Wilson stated that the fees discouraged Indian students from seeking data engineering jobs in the US, leading him to visit India for job opportunities. He acknowledged the global talent pool and highlighted the importance of immigration and new ideas for American innovation.

articles.title: Bengal BJP govt’s first month: From anti-corruption drive, border fencing to new welfare schemes | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The newly formed BJP government in West Bengal has taken several significant steps in its first month, including transferring land to the Border Security Force for border fencing and expanding the state's flagship subsidized food program.  The government has also launched an anti-corruption drive, arresting over 300 TMC leaders accused of corruption. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has promised to tackle issues like illegal infiltration and address concerns about welfare schemes. However, the government has faced criticism for its "bulldozer culture" approach to evicting street hawkers without proper rehabilitation.  The BJP government is still in its early stages and faces a long road ahead.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mass arrests without due process raise concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: Meat shops out of Varanasi? New civic body plan has traders and Opposition up in arms | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has proposed relocating meat, fish, and poultry shops to the city's outskirts, citing hygiene concerns and preservation of religious character. The proposal, approved by the executive committee and municipal corporation, aims to create designated markets with proper facilities. However, the move has sparked criticism from opposition parties and traders who argue that it will negatively impact livelihoods and inconvenience consumers.  The Samajwadi Party and UP Congress have questioned the selective action against meat shops while liquor outlets remain untouched. Traders have expressed concerns about accessibility, customer convenience, and economic losses associated with relocating their businesses. They propose alternative solutions like enclosed modern outlets or restrictions around temple areas instead of full relocation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: It potentially restricts livelihoods and raises concerns about religious imposition.

articles.title: US visa interview in 10 days if you pay extra $750: All you need to know - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department will launch a pilot program offering expedited B1/B2 visa appointments for $750, allowing applicants to schedule interviews within 10 days. This fee-based service runs from July 1, 2026, to December 31, 2026, and is only available to those seeking tourism or business travel visas. The program will not expedite the visa processing time but provides a faster interview appointment. Immigration attorneys believe this new option could be beneficial for individuals with urgent business meetings in the US.

articles.title: Punjab On Path To Becoming Startup Hub Of India: Bhagwant Mann
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann distributed seed grants worth Rs 1.07 crore to 31 startups and their founders in Punjab, aiming to support the state's burgeoning entrepreneurial ecosystem.  He emphasized that these grants, part of the Punjab Startup and Industrial Policy 2026, will help create jobs and wealth within the region. Mann highlighted the importance of innovation for economic growth, citing examples like the success of companies like Zomato, Ola, and Flipkart founded by Punjabis. He also drew parallels between entrepreneurship and governance, emphasizing that Punjab is on a path to becoming India's startup hub.

articles.title: India Adds More Nuclear Warheads: Where Do Pakistan, China Stand?
articles.rephrased_article: Russia and the United States continue to dominate the global nuclear landscape, holding 4,400 and 3,700 warheads respectively.  China saw its arsenal grow by 20 warheads, reaching 620, while India and North Korea each increased their stockpiles by 10 warheads to 190 and 60, respectively. The global nuclear landscape is characterized by a concentrated presence among major powers, with Russia boasting the most extensive network of uranium enrichment and reprocessing facilities.  Beyond stockpiles, the geography of nuclear capability reveals a strategic spread across continents.

articles.title: India had a $90 billion defence bill in 2025. Only 4 countries spent more | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: India spent $92.1 billion on its military in 2025, the fifth highest globally, according to a report by Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI).  The report highlighted an "unusually severe military crisis" between India and Pakistan in May 2025, noting that both sides used cyberattacks for the first time during the conflict. The report also stated that global military spending reached a record $2.9 trillion in 2025, with the US leading at $954 billion.  The world's nine largest nuclear weapon states held approximately 12,187 warheads at the start of 2026.

articles.title: Delhi Aims To Clear Drains By June 15 To Curb Waterlogging This Monsoon
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi's DDA reports nearly 70% completion of desilting work in stormwater drains, aiming to finish the remaining tasks by June 15th.  This effort is part of a broader city-wide initiative to prevent waterlogging during the monsoon season. The DDA claims to have completed desilting across 69 kilometers in Narela and 192 kilometers in Dwarka, removing accumulated silt, debris, vegetation, and other obstructions that can restrict rainwater flow.  The June 15 deadline is intended to ensure key drainage infrastructure is ready before the arrival of sustained monsoon rainfall.  However, whether these preparations will be sufficient remains to be seen as Delhi's annual waterlogging challenge continues to persist.

articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan, Madhya Pradesh, KC Venugopal: Rajya Sabha Pick Meenakshi Natarajan's Nomination Junked, Congress Protests
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission rejected the nomination of Meenakshi Natarajan, a Congress candidate, for the Rajya Sabha election due to her failure to disclose a pending case against her in her nomination papers.  Natarajan accused the BJP of manipulating the election and undermining democracy. The Congress protested the decision but was unsuccessful. The Election Commission has accepted a memorandum from the Congress and will seek a report from the Returning Officer, who is expected to meet with the party tomorrow.

articles.title: Why are Nigeria-South Africa tensions rising amid xenophobic attacks? | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nigeria and South Africa are experiencing heightened tensions due to escalating xenophobic attacks against Nigerians in South Africa.  Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, Nigeria's Foreign Minister, accused the South African government of failing to adequately address violence against Nigerian nationals, prompting retaliatory measures to be considered. Cyril Ramaphosa, South Africa’s President, announced new immigration policies aimed at tackling irregular migration, including stricter penalties for employers hiring undocumented workers and a new biometric registration system.  Ghana has begun repatriating its citizens from South Africa, while Mozambique has also seen a significant number of its nationals return home. This is not the first time tensions between the two countries have risen over anti-immigration sentiment.

articles.title: UK government ‘concerned’ by abuse claims against West Ham co-owner | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government expressed concern over allegations of sexual exploitation and predatory behavior against David Sullivan, co-owner of West Ham football club.  Sullivan, who recently resigned as joint chair of the club, denies the claims made by seven women. The Metropolitan Police are investigating a report relating to indecent images and sexual exploitation in the 1980s. The BBC is also investigating allegations that former editor-in-chief of the Daily Sport and Sunday Sport, Tony Livesey, facilitated a meeting between Sullivan and one of his accusers. The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) has contacted West Ham about the allegations.

articles.title: As logjam over Bengaluru development portfolio continues, insiders point fingers at CM Shivakumar | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna Byre Gowda, the newly appointed Bengaluru development minister, has yet to assume his role five days after appointment due to confusion over the scope of his portfolio.  D K Shivakumar, the Karnataka Chief Minister, retained control over key agencies like the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) and the Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), sparking dissent from senior leader Ramalinga Reddy. Despite initial disagreements, Reddy has since taken charge of the irrigation ministry.  Gowda, who was in Delhi on Tuesday, has not commented on the delay.

articles.title: Trump says in ‘final throes’ of peace deal but at least 8 killed in Lebanon | Benjamin Netanyahu News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that a peace deal with Iran is imminent, but Israeli attacks on Tyre in southern Lebanon have killed at least eight people and forced thousands to flee.  Israel claims it will continue to target southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Iran. The US president warned Netanyahu that he would be on his own if attacks continue, while Iran has threatened "more severe and crushing measures" if the fighting continues.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Escalating violence and civilian casualties in Lebanon raise serious concerns.

articles.title: Should You Stop Using Olive Oil? New Cancer Study Sparks Concern
articles.rephrased_article: A recent study from Yale School of Medicine suggests that some fats, particularly oleic acid found in olive oil and avocado, may promote pancreatic cancer tumor growth.  The research, published in Cancer Discovery, involved genetically modified mice fed high-fat diets with varying compositions. While oleic acid is traditionally considered a healthy fat for cardiovascular health, the study found it accelerated tumor growth in mice. However, omega-3 fatty acids were found to be protective against tumor growth. Experts caution that this single study does not conclusively link these oils to pancreatic cancer development and emphasize the importance of balanced diets and overall lifestyle choices.

articles.title: Promoter sells Rs 1,024 crore worth of Ajanta Pharma shares in block deal to Kotak MF and ABSL MF - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ajanta Pharma saw significant share purchases by Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund. The transactions, executed at a price of Rs 2,968 per share, reflect investor confidence in the company's strong performance.  The pharmaceutical company has benefited from steady earnings growth, healthy margins, and a robust balance sheet.

articles.title: Modi is using a cannon to kill a cockroach | Narendra Modi | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government has taken action against a satirical parody account called "Cockroach Janta Party" after it gained popularity online. The Chief Justice Surya Kant made a comparison to cockroaches and parasites, which sparked the creation of the account.  The government has pressured the page to be removed from social media platforms, accusing its founder of being influenced by foreign powers. This action is seen as an overreaction to harmless satire and reflects the growing discontent among young Indians who are facing challenges such as unemployment, climate change, and a lack of trust in their government.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Government silencing dissent through pressure on social media is a serious concern.

articles.title: World Leaders Praise PM Modi As He Becomes India's Longest-Serving Prime Minister
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi etched his name into India's political history books on Tuesday, surpassing Jawaharlal Nehru's record to become the country's longest-serving elected Prime Minister.  World leaders praised his transformative domestic governance and growing influence on the global stage. Sri Lanka's President Anura Kumara Disanayaka, Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape, and Trinidad and Tobago's Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar all sent messages of congratulations, recognizing India's transformed stature under Modi's leadership.

articles.title: Russia's fuel crisis intensifies as Ukraine steps up strikes on occupied territories
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's sustained drone attacks on Russian-occupied territories are disrupting Moscow's fuel supply lines, intensifying a crisis already triggered by long-range strikes on Russia's oil refineries.  The Crimea peninsula is experiencing severe logistical difficulties and shortages due to these attacks, with residents facing long queues for fuel and limited access. The Kremlin has acknowledged temporary difficulties in fuel supplies, attributing them to enemy air attacks. Ukrainian forces have targeted key roads and bridges connecting Crimea to mainland Russia, disrupting the flow of military and civilian goods.  The strikes are also impacting Russia's ability to fight, according to analysts.

articles.title: Deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir: What’s going on? | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Deadly protests erupted in Pakistan-administered Kashmir's Rawalakot city, resulting in the deaths of eleven people and over 70 injuries. The unrest is fueled by a ban on the Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which advocates for the abolition of reserved seats for refugees from Indian-administered Kashmir.  The JAAC claims these seats are unconstitutional, while authorities argue they are protected under the region's constitution. Sardar Waheed Khan, commissioner of the Pakistan side of the Poonch district, stated that police officers and a passerby were killed after being shot by protesters. The protests have been met with restrictions on travel and internet access.  Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, chairman of the Pakistan Peoples’ Party (PPP), has pledged to meet Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to discuss the situation.

articles.title: 300 migrants bound for UK kidnapped and threatened with kidney removal
articles.rephrased_article: The BBC has uncovered evidence of a kidnapping and torture ring operating in Libya, targeting migrants from Iraqi Kurdistan. Noah Aaron, an Iraqi Kurd smuggler who was sentenced to 10 years in France for money laundering and smuggling offenses, is believed to have been involved in the operation. The group kidnapped over 300 migrants last summer, demanding a ransom of $5,000 (£3,700) from each family.  The victims were held in cramped conditions and threatened with forced organ removal if payment was not made promptly. While some hostages were released, many remain missing or have been subjected to torture, including burning their legs and forcing them to sleep standing up for months. Anthony Dunkerley, a UN adviser who has investigated human trafficking in Libya, notes that the lack of state control in the country allows criminal groups to exploit migrants.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Kidnapping, torture, and organ trafficking are serious crimes against humanity.

articles.title: Did Netanyahu really ‘defy’ Trump in bombing Iran? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The recent escalation of hostilities between Israel and Iran has exposed growing divisions between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump, highlighting divergent interests.  Despite past praise for each other, the conflict has revealed a transactional relationship where Trump's domestic political pressures outweigh his support for Israel's military actions. While Trump aims to secure a quick deal with Iran, Netanyahu prioritizes maintaining public support for continued military action against Iran and Hezbollah in Lebanon.  Analysts suggest this clash is driven by their own political interests and the US's growing commitment to diplomacy with Tehran. The situation leaves Netanyahu facing pressure from both domestic factions and international concerns about his conduct in Gaza, while Trump faces criticism for his approach to the conflict.

articles.title: US visa interview in 10 days if you pay extra $750: All you need to know - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department will launch a pilot program offering expedited B1/B2 visa appointments for $750, allowing applicants to schedule interviews within 10 days. This fee-based service, running from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026, is limited to tourism or business travelers and does not expedite the overall visa processing time.  Immigration attorneys believe this premium service will be attractive to those with urgent business meetings in the US.

articles.title: Sea drone rescues US army helicopter crew near Strait of Hormuz
articles.rephrased_article: Two US Army helicopter crew members were rescued after their AH-64 Apache crashed near the Strait of Hormuz. The rescue was conducted by an uncrewed surface drone operated by US 5th Fleet's Task Force 59, which was launched in 2024 to bolster maritime security in the Middle East region.  The incident is under investigation and US President Donald Trump confirmed the crew members were "fine."

articles.title: Six countries sanction enablers of settler violence in occupied West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Six countries—the UK, Australia, Canada, France, New Zealand, and Norway—imposed coordinated sanctions targeting networks involved in financing, enabling, and carrying out settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. The move followed record illegal settlement expansion and rising violence by settlers.  The countries warned that they are prepared to take further measures if the Israeli government fails to address the situation on the ground. Israel's foreign ministry denounced the sanctions as politically motivated attempts to impose a stance on Jewish settlements in the West Bank, while Amnesty International called for stronger action against those who support and sponsor settler violence.

articles.title: Two held for posing as Kala Jathedi gang members to issue extortion threat to Delhi businessman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police arrested two Haryana-based businessmen, Rajan Kalra (26) and Sahil Garg (38), for allegedly impersonating members of the notorious Kala Jathedi gang and extorting money from a Delhi businessman.  The accused used international and Indian phone numbers to threaten Rohit Jain, who had an ongoing dispute with Garg over a disputed ₹2.95 crore payment. Police recovered two mobile phones from Kalra and another from Garg during raids in Haryana. The case was registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for extortion and criminal intimidation.

articles.title: Haryana sets December 2027 deadline for Yamuna pollution-control projects; Chief Secretary reviews progress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi directed all departments to accelerate the implementation of sewage-treatment, industrial-effluent-management, and pollution-control projects to improve water quality in the Yamuna.  The review meeting highlighted significant progress on new STPs, CETPs, micro-STPs, and effluent-tapping infrastructure across the Yamuna catchment. Haryana State Pollution Control Board Chairman Vinay Pratap Singh reported that projects involving over 425 MLD of additional sewage treatment capacity and over 150 MLD of industrial effluent treatment capacity are underway.  The Chief Secretary emphasized the need for strict compliance with discharge standards, regular monitoring, and stronger enforcement measures to prevent illegal dumping and unauthorized discharges.

articles.title: Exclusive: Get Bruvi’s Pod Coffee Maker for Nearly Half Off | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: WIRED is offering a discounted bundle of the Bruvi BV-01 pod coffee maker and a sampler pack of biodegradable B-Pods for $198, matching the lowest price ever tracked. The bundle usually sells for $398 and features a large touchscreen, upscale design, and wide variety of biodegradable pods.  The Bruvi is praised for its speed, efficiency, and eco-friendly waste management system.

articles.title: Schoolchildren participate in TVK function in Salem district; Education department launches inquiry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's School Education Department has launched an inquiry into allegations that students from Kuralnatham Government Primary School were forced to attend a political function organized by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Sunday. The headmaster, Deivanayagam, allegedly brought around 50 students in school uniforms to the event at Thippampatti, where they waited for the arrival of the TVK MLA, Palanivel. Following public outcry from DMK functionaries, Salem Chief Educational Officer (CEO) P. Maheswari ordered an investigation into the incident and is awaiting the report's findings.

articles.title: Threats Against Politicians Skyrocketed After Meta Changed Its Speech Rules | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta overhauled its content moderation rules last year, claiming to relax restrictions and promote free speech.  A new report from the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) found that abusive and racist comments targeting lawmakers tripled in the six months after the changes. The report also documented a significant increase in threats against President Trump and other hateful content. While Meta maintains its decision was driven by free speech principles, experts argue that relaxing moderation has led to an amplification of harmful content, potentially contributing to increased political violence and harassment.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Increased threats against politicians signal a potential threat to democracy.

articles.title: T.N. govt. must ensure senior citizens are provided safe shelter, food, and medical care: Tamilisai Soundararajan - The Hindu

articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Tamilisai Soundararajan, BJP leader, expressed deep concern over the suicides of three elderly persons in Namakkal and urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to address the issue by identifying vulnerable seniors and providing them with support services.  She called for government action to ensure adequate care, including shelter, food, medical attention, and emotional assistance.
