articles.title: Asteroid alert! NASA tracks two aeroplane-sized asteroids passing Earth today; know if they pose any risk | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA and other space agencies are tracking two near-Earth objects, 2026 LD and 2026 KM3, as they pass Earth at distances measured in millions of kilometers. While these objects are described as "aeroplane-sized," their flybys are routine encounters within the safe, non-threatening range classified by planetary defense systems.  The tracking itself is crucial for refining orbital models and predicting asteroid trajectories years or even decades ahead.

articles.title: UK to deploy AI legal assistants in Crown courts to tackle record case backlog | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government will trial artificial intelligence-powered legal assistants in Crown Courts to address a record backlog of criminal cases.  Justice Secretary David Lammy plans to announce the initiative at London Tech Week, highlighting AI's potential to modernize the justice system and deliver faster outcomes for victims. The technology is expected to analyze case files, identify cases ready for trial, and group similar hearings together. Legal bodies have welcomed the pilot but stressed the importance of thorough evaluation and investment in courts and staffing.

articles.title: More than bones: German students buried their classroom skeleton after discovering it was a real person, likely from India | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: In Schleiden, Germany, a skeleton that had been used as a teaching aid in a biology classroom for decades was recently buried after students discovered it likely originated from India. The discovery led to an investigation into the forgotten global trade of human skeletons that supplied anatomical specimens to institutions across Europe and North America during the 19th and 20th centuries.  The trade, fueled by the growing demand for real human remains in medical education, was largely unregulated and often involved individuals who died from ordinary causes without clear consent or documentation. The skeleton's journey highlights ethical concerns surrounding the use of human remains in educational settings and raises questions about ownership, consent, and the treatment of the dead.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Greta Thunberg: “Some people say that the climate crisis is something we have all created. But that is just another convenient lie. Because...” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Greta Thunberg's quote, "Some people say that the climate crisis is something we have all created. But that is just another convenient lie. Because if everyone is guilty then no one is to blame," challenges the notion of equal responsibility for climate change. The quote highlights the importance of examining power structures and systemic factors in driving environmental issues rather than solely focusing on individual actions.  While personal choices are important, Thunberg argues that meaningful progress requires addressing the institutions and decisions made at a larger scale. This principle extends beyond climate change to other areas where accountability is crucial for understanding and addressing problems.

articles.title: CBI arrests two key accused in ‘cyber-slavery’ scam case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested two individuals, Nipender Chaudhary and Nilesh Narpatsinh Purohit, for their involvement in a human trafficking network that lured Indian nationals to scam compounds in Southeast Asia. The accused allegedly arranged transportation from Thailand to Myanmar, where victims were forced into illegal cybercrime activities.  The CBI also stated that the scam compounds are run by transnational cybercrime syndicates and serve as hubs for large-scale financial fraud targeting victims across multiple countries.

articles.title: Youth from minority communities secure job placements at TGMFC job mela - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Minorities Finance Corporation (TGMFC) organized a job mela in Hyderabad on Tuesday, June 9, 2026, that saw over 80 companies participate and offer opportunities to nearly 2,000 youth. Minister for Minorities Welfare and Public Enterprise Mohammed Azharuddin and Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar inaugurated the event, emphasizing the state government's commitment to increasing employment opportunities for minority youth through skill development initiatives.  The TGMFC Chairman, Obedullah Kotwal, congratulated the selected candidates and promised another job mela in the near future.

articles.title: North Belfast Stabbing: North Belfast attack: Man arrested after stabbing leaves victim seriously injured | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A man in his 40s was seriously injured in a stabbing incident on Kinnaird Avenue in north Belfast, prompting a major police investigation. The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) declared the incident a critical incident due to its severity and impact on the community. A man in his 30s was arrested at the scene on suspicion of attempted murder and remains in custody.  Assistant Chief Constable Ryan Henderson praised bystanders who intervened during the attack, while urging the public not to share graphic footage online. The PSNI is appealing for witnesses and anyone with video evidence to come forward.

articles.title: From Hum Aapke Hain Koun to Dedh Ishqiya: Madhuri Dixit’s performances worth revisiting | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Madhuri Dixit, a beloved Bollywood star, has built a filmography that continues to resonate with audiences across generations.  Her iconic performances in films like "Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!," "Dil To Pagal Hai," and "Devdas" have cemented her place as one of the most celebrated actresses in Indian cinema. Madhuri's career spans over four decades, showcasing her versatility and enduring appeal.

articles.title: The Untold Story of the Google Buses That Took Over San Francisco | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Activists in San Francisco's Mission District, led by Supervisor David Campos, opposed new housing construction, arguing it fueled rising rents. Google employee Cari Spivack created commuter shuttles to address traffic congestion for employees living in the city. These buses became a symbol of gentrification and sparked protests from residents who felt displaced by the influx of tech workers and their luxury vehicles. The situation escalated when Google, Facebook, and other tech companies refused to share bus schedules with the city, leading to confrontations with officials like Gillian Gillett, who worked for Mayor Ed Lee.  After public pressure and a confrontation with Gillett at a meeting, the tech companies agreed to work with the city on transportation solutions.

articles.title: Trinamool, Abhishek Banerjee offices searched in signature forgery case | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal CID conducted searches at the Trinamool Congress's central office in Kolkata and Abhishek Banerjee's office on Camac Street as part of its investigation into alleged Assembly signature forgery.  The searches followed a complaint filed by rebel TMC MLAs Ritabrata Banerjee and Sandipan Saha alleging fabricated signatures on a letter sent to the Assembly Speaker regarding the appointment of the Leader of Opposition. The CID has recorded statements from 13 TMC MLAs, with three disowning the signatures attributed to them. Abhishek Banerjee skipped a third summons issued by the Crime Investigation Department citing pending proceedings before the Calcutta High Court and his absence from the city.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Isaac Newton: “A man may imagine things that are false, but he can only understand things that are true.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Isaac Newton, a renowned scientist, emphasized the distinction between imagination and understanding in his quote: "A man may imagine things that are false, but he can only understand things that are true."  He highlighted that while imagination is powerful and allows for creative thinking, it doesn't guarantee truth. Understanding requires evidence and testing to ensure accuracy. This principle applies not just to scientific discoveries but also to everyday life, urging individuals to critically evaluate information and distinguish between assumptions and reality.

articles.title: Deep-sea radioactive waste mystery: Scientists begin hunt for 200,000 nuclear barrels dumped in the Atlantic Ocean | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An international team of scientists is conducting the most detailed investigation yet of over 200,000 barrels of radioactive waste dumped in the Atlantic Ocean decades ago. Using autonomous underwater vehicles, they are mapping the seabed and assessing the condition of the containers to determine if any radioactive materials have escaped into the surrounding environment. The mission aims to understand how these barrels have changed on the seafloor and their potential impact on nearby ecosystems. This investigation could shed light on a question that has remained unanswered for more than 30 years: what became of the radioactive waste that the world left behind.

articles.title: Sikkim Suicide Rate Falls 15.8% In 2 Years As Focus On Mental Health Expands
articles.rephrased_article: Sikkim has experienced a 15.8% decline in its suicide rate over two years, according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data. The rate dropped from 43.1 per lakh population in 2022 to 36.3 in 2024.  Sikkim Health Minister GT Dhungel attributed this improvement to collaborative efforts by various departments, mental health professionals, schools, NGOs, local bodies, police personnel and community groups. He emphasized the importance of sustained mental health interventions and community support for further reducing suicides and improving access to care in the state.

articles.title: What happened when China’s Xi Jinping visited North Korea for first time in 7 years | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un met in Pyongyang, marking a new chapter in their bilateral ties. The leaders agreed to expand cooperation across politics, economy, and culture, with China emphasizing practical state-to-state ties and its vision for international order. While the summit focused on strengthening economic and cultural alliances, North Korea's official summary framed the meeting as one between equal partners, omitting any mention of nuclear weapons or US relations.  Despite the display of goodwill, analysts noted that the two countries' official summaries reflected different priorities.

articles.title: Police file chargesheet in Aluva Athul murder case in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karunagappally police filed a comprehensive chargesheet in the Aluva Athul murder case, alleging that the victim was killed due to a long-standing feud between his group and an organized criminal gang. The chargesheet, prepared based on solid scientific evidence and rigorous field investigation, includes over 50 site and recovery memos, seized vehicles, and more than 100 pieces of material evidence.  The police successfully tracked down and arrested 13 out of the 15 accused within 24 hours of the crime, with the remaining two apprehended for destroying crucial CCTV footage. The investigation also relied on digital footprints from over 50 surveillance cameras and mobile phone records to establish a timeline of the conspiracy and execution of the murder.

articles.title: Why Trump's Attention May Become Pak's Biggest Headache
articles.rephrased_article:
Pakistan's renewed relevance under President Trump has brought challenges, particularly regarding his desire to revive the Abraham Accords and his unpredictable foreign policy.  Trump's praise for Pakistani leadership can be conditional and temporary, creating vulnerabilities for Pakistan as its economy relies on Western influence. The country faces risks from potential tensions with Iran and a need to balance relations with both the US and China. 
Pakistan's current diplomatic success may not translate into long-term stability due to Trump's transactional approach to foreign policy.  The relationship appears superficial, lacking depth or genuine warmth.

articles.title: Modi at 4,399 Days: The making of India’s longest-serving elected prime minister | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi has surpassed Jawaharlal Nehru's record for the longest tenure as India's elected Prime Minister, achieving 4,399 days in office. Since assuming power in 2014, he has secured three consecutive mandates and led a period of significant economic growth and national development.  His leadership has been marked by initiatives like Swachh Bharat, Ayushman Bharat, and digital governance reforms, as well as assertive foreign policy stances that have strengthened India's global standing. The writer believes Modi is the "Man of Destiny for India" who will shape the country's future as "Swarnim Bharat."

articles.title: Passports Held, Coerced Into Scams: How "Cyber Slavery" Gang Lured Indians
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested two key accused, Nipender Chaudhary and Nilesh Narpatsinh Purohit, in connection with a human trafficking network that lured Indian nationals into cybercrime operations in Southeast Asia. articles.title: Deep-sea radioactive waste mystery: Scientists begin hunt for 200,000 nuclear barrels dumped in the Atlantic Ocean | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An international team is conducting a detailed investigation of the Atlantic Ocean's deep-sea dumping grounds, where over 200,000 barrels of radioactive waste were deposited decades ago.  The French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) and the Nuclear Ocean Dump Site Survey Monitoring project (NODSSUM) are using autonomous underwater vehicles to locate the barrels, which have never been precisely mapped. The mission aims to assess the condition of the containers and their potential impact on nearby ecosystems. Researchers hope to understand how radioactive substances behave in deep marine environments over long periods and improve understanding of radionuclide transport, deep-sea ecology, and the lasting environmental legacy of twentieth-century nuclear policies.

articles.title: Kuwait caps domestic worker hiring at 10 countries, restricts recruiting from 27 others | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kuwait has implemented new regulations governing domestic worker recruitment, restricting the list of approved source countries to 10. The Ministry of Interior issued a circular outlining updated procedures, including restrictions on recruitment from 27 countries, based on assessments by various government agencies.  Recruitment will now be handled through governorate-level service centres and is permitted for domestic workers from South Africa, Benin, Eritrea, Ethiopia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, India, Vietnam, and Nepal. The new regulations have come into effect.

articles.title: Worli Concert Death: After Mumbai Concert Death, Spotlight On Drugs, Safety Lapses
articles.rephrased_article: A 28-year-old law student, Vrishabh Mahendra Gangurde, died at a techno concert in Mumbai after reportedly consuming excessive alcohol and possibly banned substances.  Space Bound, the event organizer, along with its CEO Karan Singh and senior manager Parag Oke, have been booked for negligence under Indian law. This incident follows similar cases of drug-related deaths at music events across Mumbai and Pune, highlighting a concerning trend of substance abuse and potential negligence at large gatherings.  Authorities are struggling to monitor the risks associated with these events despite increased enforcement efforts.

articles.title: Woman misses hospital visit as KSRTC bus departs before time, gets Rs 35,000 compensation | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kerala ordered the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) to pay compensation and costs to a woman who missed a reserved bus due to its departure before schedule. The commission found that the KSRTC failed to provide the service at the scheduled time, causing a deficiency in service as per the Consumer Protection Act.  The commission ordered the corporation to refund the bus fare, pay compensation, and cover costs.

articles.title: Congress MLAs Stranded At Bhopal Airport Over Plane Mix-up
articles.rephrased_article: Congress MLAs and their families faced confusion at Bhopal Airport due to a smaller aircraft than expected for their travel to Bengaluru. The Congress had arranged two batches of flights, with the first flight accommodating 76 MLAs and family members, while another was planned later in the evening for the remaining MLAs.  The move came amid heightened political tension after the BJP fielded Mahesh Kevat as a candidate for the Rajya Sabha seat against Congress's Meenakshi Natarajan. The Congress is concerned about potential cross-voting and has decided to send its MLAs to Karnataka.

articles.title: Who will fly on Artemis 3? Nasa set to reveal crew for next major moon mission | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Nasa is expected to announce the crew for its Artemis 3 mission on Tuesday. Strong contenders include Raja Chari, Nicole Mann, Kayla Barron, and Andre Douglas. While the final selection remains secret until the official announcement, these names consistently appear at the top of expert predictions.

articles.title: Kuwait caps domestic worker hiring at 10 countries, restricts recruiting from 27 others | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kuwait has introduced new regulations governing the recruitment of domestic workers, limiting approved source countries to 10 and restricting recruitment from dozens more. The Ministry of Interior issued a circular outlining updated procedures, including recruitment through governorate-level service centres.  The changes are aimed at regulating the sector and streamlining the process, with restrictions based on assessments by various government agencies. All recruitment procedures will be handled through these centers, effective immediately.

articles.title: India World's 5th Largest Military Spender With $92 Billion War Chest: Report
articles.rephrased_article: India ranked fifth in global military spending at $92.1 billion in 2025, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI).  The country's nuclear arsenal grew slightly to approximately 190 warheads by January 2026, surpassing Pakistan's 170. Global military spending rose to $2.9 trillion in 2025, marking the eleventh consecutive annual increase. SIPRI also noted that several regional flashpoints remained at risk of escalating into major interstate armed conflicts.

articles.title: Quote of the day by American investor Ray Dalio: “If you’re not failing, you’re not pushing your limits, and if you’re not pushing your limits, you’re not...” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ray Dalio, a successful investor, argues that failure is not to be feared but embraced as a necessary component of growth.  He suggests that individuals who avoid mistakes may be staying within their comfort zones and missing out on opportunities for significant personal development. While many people fear failure and avoid taking risks, Dalio believes that setbacks can provide valuable lessons and insights that lead to greater success. His perspective is based on his own experiences in the unforgiving world of financial markets where he learned to embrace uncertainty and adapt his strategies accordingly.  He emphasizes that embracing failure allows individuals to push their limits, learn from mistakes, and ultimately achieve their full potential.

articles.title: Iran says US has revoked World Cup ticket allocation for their supporters | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s football federation claims the United States has revoked its allocation of World Cup tickets for Iranian supporters, accusing the cohost of obstructing their attendance due to diplomatic tensions. The federation stated that FIFA regulations require 8 percent of tickets be allocated to each participating team for distribution to fans through official channels. FFIRI, which had already begun ticket sales for Iran’s group stage matches against New Zealand, Belgium and Egypt, claims it is unable to provide any tickets due to the withdrawal of the allocation.  Neither FIFA nor US organizers have publicly commented on the Iranian accusation.

articles.title: Over 30 Dead, 200 Injured As Security Forces Open Fire On Protesters In PoK
articles.rephrased_article: Over 30 people were killed and around 200 injured in clashes between protesters and security forces in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) after authorities banned the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a prominent civil society alliance. The ban was issued due to concerns over public order and security, following the death of a trader allegedly shot by law enforcement.  The clashes erupted in Rawalakot after tensions flared over the trader's death, with JAAC supporters using automatic rifles, petrol bombs, and other weapons against security forces. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) condemned the use of excessive force and called for dialogue and transparent grievance addressing.

articles.title: Trump courts boos at historic New York NBA Finals appearance | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's appearance at Madison Square Garden for the NBA Finals drew boos from sections of the crowd and triggered a large security operation.  The event, which was supposed to be a historic moment with the first sitting president attending an NBA game, became overshadowed by political undertones. Trump, who watched from an executive suite, was met with jeers during the national anthem, highlighting the country's deep divisions. Despite the security measures and heightened tension, the night featured celebrity sightings and a star-studded atmosphere.

articles.title: Kenya police fire tear gas at protest against US Ebola quarantine centre plan in Nanyuki
articles.rephrased_article: Kenyan police used tear gas to disperse a protest in Nanyuki against the construction of an Ebola quarantine center for US citizens. Protesters, who were demanding the plan be reversed, expressed concerns about cross-border infection risks and lack of transparency from the government. President William Ruto defended the plan, stating that it was necessary due to proximity and the need for timely treatment.  The High Court had previously halted the facility's opening but construction continued despite this ruling.

articles.title: Are Ronaldo, Messi still the largest World Cup draws, or is Mbappe bigger? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The popularity of football's biggest stars, Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, and Kylian Mbappe, is being debated ahead of the 2026 World Cup. While all three are household names, Mbappe has emerged as a contender for mainstream appeal with his impressive goal-scoring record at a young age.  Messi and Ronaldo have already dominated global sporting events, but Mbappe's recent success in La Liga has propelled him to the forefront of the conversation. Ticket sales, social media following, and regular season statistics all point towards Mbappe's growing influence.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Iran fan ticket allocation revoked, says FFIRI - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Fifa has revoked Iran's allocation of fan tickets for the World Cup group stage, citing regulations that require each participating federation to receive 8% of tickets. The Iranian Football Federation (FFIRI) claims this decision violates international competition principles and raises concerns about political interference.  The FFIRI is calling on Fifa to uphold neutrality and fairness in the organization of the tournament.

articles.title: Russian attacks kill 5 in Ukraine as Zelenskyy hails talks with US envoys | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zelenskyy expressed hope to reinvigorate diplomacy after "very positive" talks with US envoys and European leaders, who discussed how to coordinate support for Ukraine.  The attacks in the Kharkiv region killed five people, including a pregnant woman, while two others were killed in Donetsk. A drone attack injured 16 people in Kharkiv, including children. Zelenskyy also met with British, French, and German leaders about ending the war. The UK, Germany, and France reiterated their support for Ukraine and pledged to coordinate support at upcoming summits.

articles.title: Man accused of killing mother-in-law with poison-laced satay
articles.rephrased_article: Purwadi Wahyudi, a 40-year-old man in Indonesia, has been arrested for allegedly poisoning his mother-in-law, Aminah, with rat poison-laced satay.  Police say he ordered the poisoned skewers and delivered them to Aminah's house after feeling disrespected by her. The family discovered Aminah's body covered in vomit the next day and contacted police, who exhumed the body and found signs of poisoning. Indrawan Wira Saputra, head of the Boyolali police's criminal investigation unit, stated that the killing was carefully planned.

articles.title: ‘Historic’ wave of Palestinian solidarity grows at universities in Germany | Education News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A wave of Palestinian solidarity is growing at German universities, with student councils in Leipzig, Berlin, and Dusseldorf demanding the cessation of collaborations with Israeli institutions. These demands stem from accusations that Israeli universities contribute to the Israeli military complex and advance government narratives, including those related to the occupation of Palestine.  The movement has been met with resistance from some university leadership, who have cited concerns about academic freedom and student safety. Despite this pushback, students continue to organize and advocate for Palestinian rights.

articles.title: Visakhapatnam MP Sribharat reviews facilities at Dwaraka RTC Complex - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat inspected the Dwaraka RTC Complex, reviewing passenger amenities and cleanliness. He discussed hygiene standards at canteens and suggested improvements to information displays, including digital systems for real-time updates. Sribharat also noted the need for greater public awareness regarding waste disposal and aesthetic upgrades to enhance the commuter experience.

articles.title: Philippines: Hundreds of aftershocks jolt Philippines as officials say death toll could rise
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of aftershocks have continued to plague the southern Philippines since a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck on Monday, leaving dozens dead and hundreds injured.  The scale of devastation is growing as emergency responders reach affected areas. Buildings have collapsed, roads are damaged, and power and communication lines remain down in many regions. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr has mobilized the government to respond to the disaster. Science minister Renato Solidum noted that students who were attending a morning assembly at their schools survived because they were outside when the quake struck.

articles.title: Hundred days of Israel’s latest war on Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Lebanon have been engaged in direct diplomatic talks for the first time in decades, but efforts to fully implement a ceasefire have failed.  The 100-day conflict has resulted in thousands of deaths, with at least 3,600 people killed in Lebanon, according to the country's Ministry of Public Health. The fighting has also displaced over 1.2 million people from their homes.  Israel has intensified its attacks on southern Lebanon, occupying a larger area than previously and threatening Beirut.  Hezbollah, a pro-Iran political and paramilitary group, is using fiber-optic drones in the conflict, aiming to wear down Israeli forces. Iran has pledged to link any ceasefire deal with the US and Israel, while Lebanon's government seeks to maintain its authority amid pressure from the US and Israel to crack down on Hezbollah.

articles.title: Chief Minister travels by Metro to avoid Zero-Traffic arrangements in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar traveled by Namma Metro from Vidhana Soudha to Silk Institute on Sunday, June 7, 2026, to visit his home turf of Kanakapura.  He chose this method to avoid disrupting traffic for the public after recognizing the inconvenience of using zero-traffic arrangements. The decision followed a similar incident last week where Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot's convoy was granted zero-traffic access at Wind Tunnel Junction, sparking public outrage and criticism about Bengaluru's infrastructure.

articles.title: Indian diaspora groups welcome court ruling striking down $100,000 H-1B visa fee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A federal court in Massachusetts ruled that the $100,000 fee imposed by the Trump administration on H-1B visas was unlawful because it lacked congressional approval. Khanderao Kand, Chief of Policy and Strategy at the Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS), welcomed the decision, stating it restores predictability and fairness to the employment-based immigration system.  Sanjeev Joshipura, Executive Director of Indiaspora, expressed cautious optimism, noting that the administration could still impose procedural hurdles on H-1B visa holders.

articles.title: Foreigners who returned after voting in T.N. Assembly election come under the scanner - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Central and State law-enforcement agencies are collaborating with the Election Commission of India to investigate potential voter fraud in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections.  The focus is on foreign nationals of Indian origin who returned to their home countries shortly after voting, with investigators seeking assistance from the Bureau of Immigration.

articles.title: From the Vatican to the White House: The Unlikely Alliance
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV, in his first encyclical, "Magnifica Humanitas," addresses the ethical and social challenges posed by artificial intelligence (AI).  He echoes concerns raised by Leo XIII in 1891 regarding the impact of industrialization on labor. The debate over AI's benefits is intensifying with proposals from Senator Bernie Sanders, who advocates for an American AI sovereign wealth fund, and OpenAI chief Sam Altman, who suggests sharing AI-generated wealth with citizens. President Donald Trump has expressed support for similar ideas, though they face opposition from some liberal economists. The debate reflects a broader tension between the potential benefits of AI and concerns about its impact on employment and inequality.

articles.title: Haunted by 2020, Congress flies Madhya Pradesh MLAs to Karnataka before Rajya Sabha vote | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: To secure a third seat in the June 18 Rajya Sabha election, the BJP needs additional votes.  The Congress has relocated nearly all of its 61 MLAs to Karnataka, citing concerns about potential BJP attempts to contact them. The move is seen as a precautionary measure to prevent defections and maintain party unity ahead of the vote.  Congress leaders have denied any discontent among their legislators and insist they are united in supporting their nominee, Meenakshi Natarajan.

articles.title: Hungry and broke, Mithun Chakraborty asked reporter for food after National Award win | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mimoh Chakraborty, son of veteran actor Mithun Chakraborty, shared stories of his father's struggles before achieving success in Bollywood.  He recalled instances where his father slept on the streets, faced police harassment, and went hungry after winning a National Award for his debut film. These experiences have inspired Mimoh to persevere through challenges he faces in his own career. Mithun Chakraborty himself has spoken about enduring hardships while trying to establish himself in the film industry, including sleeping with an empty stomach and worrying about his next meal. He believes his journey is a testament to overcoming adversity and achieving success despite immense struggles.

articles.title: Coaching centre firing case: Patna court stays arrest of ‘Khan Sir’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Faisal Khan, also known as “Khan Sir”, a popular educator and YouTuber, was granted an interim stay on his arrest in connection with a firing incident at his coaching institute in Patna. Mr. Khan’s lawyer argued that he had no direct involvement in the incident, which stemmed from a rivalry between Khan Global Studies (KGS) and another coaching institute. The court also rejected the bail plea of Raushan Anand, the rival institute owner who was arrested alongside two others on June 2nd.  The case is scheduled for further hearing on June 12th.

articles.title: Fresh plea in Supreme Court over CBSE’s three-language rule for Class 9; seeks stay on rollout | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Fauzia Khan, an educationist and former Maharashtra minister, has filed a plea in the Supreme Court challenging the CBSE's new policy mandating the study of three languages for Class 9 students beginning July 1st. The plea argues that the policy is arbitrary and violates the National Education Policy 2020 by forcing non-Hindi states to introduce Hindi or Sanskrit without educational justification.  The CBSE, citing alignment with the NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023, has mandated the study of at least two native Indian languages alongside a third language for students opting for this new curriculum.

articles.title: Tuft & Needle Promo Codes: 30% Off | June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Tuft & Needle, a company that makes mattresses, pillows, sheets and more, is offering discounts on various sleep products. Tuft & Needle also offers discounts on their pillows, including the Zip Comfort Pillow and Original Foam Pillow, as well as sleep technology tools like white noise machines and smart alarm clocks. The company is offering up to 20% off its range of mattresses, including the T&N Original Mattress, T&N Mint Mattress, and T&N Original Hybrid Mattress. Tuft & Needle also provides a 100-day warranty policy, free shipping and returns (except in Alaska and Hawaii), and a 10-year limited warranty on its mattresses.

articles.title: Beyond Religion, Caste, Class: BJP Eyes UP Via Madhya Pradesh Rajya Sabha Seat
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP has nominated Mahesh Kewat, chairman of the Madhya Pradesh State Fisherman Welfare Board, to represent the state in the Rajya Sabha. This nomination is being interpreted as a symbolic gesture drawing on the Ramayana story of Lord Ram's boatman, Kewat, who helped him cross the river. The BJP hopes this move will resonate with Extremely Backward Classes communities and strengthen its presence in Bundelkhand, while also sending a morale-boosting message to its cadre.  This strategy could be part of a larger plan for both Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh's upcoming elections.

articles.title: Noom Promo Codes: 50% Off Best Deals & Free Trials for June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Noom, a human-to-human weight loss coaching service founded in 2008, has expanded its offerings to include GLP-1 medication support and AI coaching. The company offers various plans, including a free trial, for sustainable weight loss, habit tracking, and personalized nutrition guidance. Noom also provides GLP-1 prescriptions and access to medications like WeGovy, Ozempic, and Zepbound at varying costs depending on the plan chosen.

articles.title: Apple Tries Again On AI, Turns To Google For Help
articles.rephrased_article: Apple unveiled a major AI update for its iPhone, collaborating with Google on the technology. The new Siri AI will feature natural communication and app integration, but daily usage limits will be applied to certain features due to their reliance on powerful server models.  The rollout of Siri AI will initially exclude Europe and China as Apple works through regulatory issues. Analysts praised the company's deliberate approach to AI development, noting its potential for monetization without needing to invest billions in infrastructure like rivals.

articles.title: Power cuts leave Chennai residents fuming; protests erupt across city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Widespread power outages across Chennai from Monday night into Tuesday morning caused public outrage and protests at Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB) offices. Residents demanded immediate restoration of power supply, citing recurring issues with voltage fluctuations, single-phase supply, and complete blackouts.  Protests were reported in several areas, including Arumbakkam, Madipakkam, Washermenpet, Tiruvottiyur, Ambattur, Madhavaram, Manali, Avadi, Poonamallee, Thirunindravur, Medavakkam, and Velachery. Some residents resorted to road blockades, while others questioned the TNEB staff about the prolonged disruptions and alleged lack of response to complaints.

articles.title: OnePlus Promo Codes: 30% Off June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: OnePlus, a popular Android device maker, has launched its latest phone, the OnePlus 15, with new features and improvements. The company is also offering promotions on its other products, including the OnePlus Pad 3, OnePlus 12, OnePlus Buds 4, and OnePlus Pad Go 2. WIRED recommends the OnePlus 12 for its improved camera quality and fast charging, while praising the OnePlus Pad as a worthy iPad alternative.  The company also offers discounts on various OnePlus products through their promo code system.

articles.title: RVNL shares jump 3% after securing Rs 221 crore Railway contract - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RVNL, a railway infrastructure company, secured a Letter of Acceptance (LoA) for a signaling and infrastructure upgrade project in the Bilaspur Division of South East Central Railway. The project involves replacing conventional Panel Interlocking systems with advanced Electronic Interlocking technology at multiple stations across the division. The contract, valued at Rs 221.33 crore, will be executed under the EPC model by South East Central Railway, a domestic entity. This win strengthens RVNL's order book and positions it as a key player in India's railway modernization drive.

articles.title: Scientists baked sourdough using 5,300-year-old yeast from a frozen mummy and it actually fermented | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ötzi, the "Iceman," preserved in the Alps, has provided scientists with an unexpected opportunity to study ancient microbial life. Researchers have found evidence of cold-loving yeasts in samples from his body and surrounding environment, suggesting they may have survived for millennia in a frozen state.  While their presence is not surprising given Ötzi's environment, scientists are still debating whether these organisms represent post-mortem colonization or something more persistent that has endured through time. The study of these ancient yeasts offers potential insights into the past and could even be used to bake sourdough bread.

articles.title: Bhopal Jail Denies VIP Treatment To Ex-Judge Giribala Singh, Son Samarth In Twisha Sharma Death Case
articles.rephrased_article: Giribala Singh, a retired judge, and her son Samarth Singh, Twisha Sharma's husband, are being held in Bhopal Central Jail according to prison officials. The jail denies claims of VIP treatment for the accused, stating they are being treated like other undertrial prisoners.  The jail administration has increased security measures due to the presence of 29 individuals sentenced by Giribala Singh within the same facility. Prison Headquarters maintains that all amenities are provided strictly according to prison rules and no formal inquiry or report exists regarding the situation.

articles.title: CBI Begins Probe Into Tamil Nadu's Rs 397 Crore Transformer Tender Scam
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered an FIR following orders from the Madras High Court in response to complaints alleging corruption in Tamil Nadu's transformer procurement tenders. The case involves irregularities in the 2021, 2022 and 2023 tender processes, with allegations that the process was manipulated to favor select companies at the expense of the state exchequer. The CBI has booked officials from the Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation Limited (TANGEDCO), members of the Tender Scrutiny Committee, government employees, and private contractors on charges of corruption, cheating, and criminal conspiracy. The investigation will examine whether procurement rules were violated, if public officials misused their positions, and if there was any collusion to provide undue benefits to specific companies.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of corruption in a large-scale government tender raise serious concerns about abuse of power.

articles.title: When is the longest day of the year 2026: Know exact date, science behind the summer solstice, and what it means | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The summer solstice, a precise astronomical moment defined by the Earth's axial tilt and its position relative to the Sun, occurs at 4:24 am EDT on June 21, 2026. While the Northern Hemisphere experiences the longest day of sunlight, daylight duration varies across latitudes and time zones. Stonehenge in England aligns with the Sun's position during sunrise on the solstice, attracting visitors who celebrate its significance as a marker of the changing seasons.  However, the summer solstice is not always marked by dramatic changes in weather or visibility, as the difference between day and night is subtle for most observers.

articles.title: Italian commuters find a moment of peace on a cable-guided ferry sketched by Leonardo da Vinci - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Leonardo's Ferry, a reaction ferry designed centuries ago and immortalized by Leonardo da Vinci, has returned to its original purpose of connecting two populations on the Adda River.  The ferry, operated by the town of Imbersago, provides a unique alternative route for commuters due to a nearby bridge closure. Volunteers now run the service, offering passengers a scenic three-minute respite from their daily commutes. Passengers pay a fee based on vehicle type and are able to enjoy the river's beauty while traveling.

articles.title: Adani Energy Signs Pact To Buy Smart Meter Firm IntelliSmart For Rs 3,050 Crore
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) announced the acquisition of 100% stake in IntelliSmart Infrastructure Private Limited for Rs 3,050 crore. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

articles.title: Meet Ravi Vij: Indian-origin cancer specialist honoured with a prestigious US professorship for redefining blood cancer treatment | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ravi Vij, an Indian-origin physician-scientist, has been named the inaugural Jeffrey S. and Prue H. Gershman Distinguished Professor at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis.  His career has focused on advancing treatment options for multiple myeloma and other blood cancers, including leading clinical trials that explored innovative immunotherapy approaches and stem cell transplant strategies. Vij's research has contributed to a growing field of precision medicine and he has mentored 25 early-career researchers. His work has been recognized by the American Society of Clinical Oncology and the American Society of Hematology, where he currently serves as senior editor of the journal *Clinical Lymphoma, Myeloma and Leukemia*.  His appointment highlights his contributions to cancer research, patient care, and medical education.

articles.title: Karnataka Man, 24, Invited To Birthday Party, Strangled, Body Burnt
articles.rephrased_article: A 24-year-old man, Basanagouda, was allegedly murdered in Ballari district, Karnataka after being invited to a birthday party near a canal.  Police suspect he was strangled with a rope and then set on fire by the assailants who attempted to destroy evidence of the crime. A murder case has been registered at Moka Police Station and an investigation is underway to determine the motive behind the killing.

articles.title: Iran’s lakes are vanishing: Satellite images show a deepening water crisis | Environment | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran is facing a severe water crisis due to years of drought, unsustainable water use, and damage to its water infrastructure from the US-Israel war. Satellite images show Lake Urmia, once the largest saltwater lake in the Middle East, has shrunk dramatically.  The country's reliance on agriculture for water consumption has exacerbated the problem, with over 90% of withdrawals going towards irrigation. The situation is leading to water shortages, forcing people to migrate from rural areas and straining urban centers like Tehran. While desalination plays a small role in meeting Iran's water needs, it is concentrated along its southern coast.

articles.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Israel presses deeper into Gaza as Cairo talks begin | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel continued its expansion of control into the Gaza Strip, extending earth berms along the "Yellow Line" and demolishing homes.  The Israeli army also carried out multiple airstrikes in Gaza City, Khan Younis, and Deir el-Balah, killing at least 13 Palestinians. Meanwhile, Israel closed the northern Zikim Crossing and tightened restrictions on movement in the West Bank, with settlers setting fire to farmland and olive groves.  Palestinian factions met in Cairo to discuss the second phase of the ceasefire agreement, but violence continued with the deaths of two Palestinian children by Israeli forces.

articles.title: A child's tooth and mysterious green stones expose a 5,500-year-old secret hidden in a mountain cave | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists at Cova del Sardo, a cave in the Spanish Pyrenees, have uncovered evidence of prehistoric expeditions and copper mining activities dating back 5,500 years.  The discovery includes a child's tooth, suggesting repeated visits to the site over centuries, and fragments of green minerals associated with copper deposits. These findings suggest that the cave may have served multiple functions beyond resource extraction, including potential burial sites or ritual spaces. The research pushes back evidence for human engagement with copper resources in this part of the Iberian Peninsula, but many questions remain unanswered about the motivations behind people's repeated visits to the remote location.

articles.title: Wembanyama scores 32 as Spurs power past Knicks in Game 3 of NBA Finals | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks 115-111 in Game 3 of the NBA Finals, snapping a 13-game winning streak for New York.  Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 32 points and eight rebounds, while Stephon Castle added 23 points. The Knicks' 13-game winning streak was snapped, but they still lead the best-of-seven series two games to one. Game 4 is scheduled for Wednesday night in New York.

articles.rephrased_article: Iran and Israel have paused their tit-for-tat attacks following a fragile ceasefire since April 8, but tensions remain high. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Iranian parliamentary speaker, criticized Israel for continued violations of the truce, warning that it could break. Donald Trump, US President, urged Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, to be cautious as further strikes risk undermining the ceasefire.  Analysts suggest the attacks were a message to Washington that Israel's security concerns cannot be ignored.

articles.title: The sheep-killer myth that helped drive the Tasmanian tiger to extinction and why scientists think farmers got it wrong | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tasmanian Land Conservancy and researchers from the School of Natural Sciences, University of Tasmania have challenged the long-held belief that the Tasmanian tiger was a devastating sheep killer. Historical records show over 2,000 bounties were paid for thylacine kills, but many accusations were based on assumptions rather than direct observation.  New research suggests that while hunting likely contributed to the species' decline, another factor, possibly an epidemic disease, may have weakened its population before persecution intensified. The extinction of the Tasmanian tiger highlights how myths, economic fears, and incomplete evidence can contribute to the demise of a species.

articles.title: China’s Xi, North Korea’s Kim pledge to boost ties at rare Pyongyang summit | Xi Jinping News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping, the President of China, and Kim Jong Un, the leader of North Korea, met in Pyongyang for a rare summit, pledging to deepen their cooperation. During the meeting, both leaders agreed to strengthen strategic communication and work together on shared interests.  They also discussed international issues and reaffirmed their commitment to the "one China principle". This visit marks Xi's first to North Korea in seven years and comes amid increasing tensions between China and the United States over trade and nuclear programs.

articles.title: RVNL shares jump 3% after securing Rs 221 crore Railway contract - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RVNL, a railway PSU, has secured a Letter of Acceptance (LoA) for a signaling and infrastructure upgrade project in the Bilaspur Division of South East Central Railway. The project involves replacing conventional Panel Interlocking systems with advanced Electronic Interlocking technology across multiple stations. The contract, awarded under the EPC model, is valued at Rs 221.33 crore and will be executed within 730 days.  The company clarified that neither its promoter group nor any group companies have any interest in the awarding entity.

articles.title: What Americans Think About US Intervention In Conflicts Abroad
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated in January that help was on its way for Iranians amid protests, assuming the Iranian people would welcome US intervention as a chance for a better future.  However, the US launched military action against Iran six weeks later, with Trump arguing it could give Iranians a chance to overthrow their government and build a better future. This strategy echoes past claims by Vice President Dick Cheney in 2003 that American troops would be "greeted as liberators" in Iraq, similar to the US's claim of support for interventions in other countries like Venezuela, Greenland, and Canada.  The success of these interventions hinges on public perception and often relies on the belief that local populations want the intervention.

articles.title: Truck carrying fireworks catches fire, sparks spectacular display
articles.rephrased_article: A truck carrying fireworks caught fire on June 6th in Chattanooga, Tennessee, causing a spectacular display of pyrotechnics that temporarily halted traffic.  The local fire department quickly extinguished the blaze, with no reported injuries. The incident occurred near the city's outskirts and left onlookers stunned by the sudden burst of colorful explosions.

articles.title: Baby Do Die Do teaser: Huma Qureshi plays death-defying deaf-mute hitwoman | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Huma Qureshi and her brother Saqib Saleem, who co-founded their production house, Saleem Siblings, have released the teaser for their crime thriller, "Baby Do Die Do." The 90-second teaser introduces Qureshi as a mysterious deaf-mute hitwoman navigating Mumbai's underbelly.  The film also stars Chunky Panday, Sikandar Kher, and Vidya Malvade. It is slated for release in cinemas on July 3rd.

articles.title: Ecuadorian artisans working to preserve the traditional craft of weaving horsehair strainers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ligia Ipiales and Guido Paucar, the last two remaining "cedacero" artisans in Guangopolo, Ecuador, are struggling to maintain a traditional craft that once sustained their village.  The decline of horsehair sourcing due to industrialization and environmental shifts has significantly impacted their ability to produce the intricate sieves, which were once essential for sifting flour in Ecuadorian kitchens. The dwindling number of weavers, coupled with the high cost of imported horsehair, threatens the future of this unique craft.  Efforts to train a new generation have proven unsuccessful, leaving Guangopolo facing the potential loss of its cultural identity.

articles.title: Oman coast: Indian crew rescued from tanker that caught fire after US strike
articles.rephrased_article: Indian crew members aboard a tanker, the MT Marivex, were rescued after it caught fire off the coast of Oman following a US strike. The incident occurred on June 8th and involved 24 Indian seafarers who had sent distress signals about the vessel's sinking.  The US Central Command stated that the tanker violated an ongoing blockade against Iran by attempting to sail to an Iranian port, prompting the strike with a precision munition.  Both the All India Seafarers Union and the Forward Seamen's Union of India confirmed the crew's safety after being evacuated by helicopter operated by Omani authorities.

articles.title: Black bear caught in Japan after days of sightings
articles.rephrased_article: Japanese authorities captured a black bear in Utsunomiya after days of sightings, following a series of attacks that reached record levels. The bear was tranquilized using three shots and weighed approximately 100kg.  Another bear is still evading capture in Fukushima, prompting officials to use drones and AI-powered systems for tracking and deterring the animal. This rise in bear encounters has led to increased efforts by local governments and companies to address the issue.

articles.title: IIT Jammu launch new interdisciplinary programmes for 2026-27
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Jammu has launched a new BTech program called Unified Engineering, designed for students seeking to explore multiple engineering disciplines. The program integrates hands-on learning across domains like AI, robotics, and sustainable energy technologies, emphasizing teamwork, innovation, and real-world problem solving. Graduates will be prepared for careers in systems engineering, product development, and AI.  This initiative is part of a broader trend of IITs expanding their BTech offerings to align with industry demands.

articles.title: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un vow stronger ties in North Korea visit
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping concluded a two-day visit to Pyongyang, his first official trip since 2019, reaffirming the strong ties between China and North Korea.  During the visit, both leaders emphasized their commitment to deepening bilateral relations and highlighted the significance of their shared history. While no concrete deals were announced, Xi Jinping expressed hope for a brighter future for both countries' socialist causes. The trip comes amid growing tensions with the US and Russia, as Kim Jong Un seeks to solidify his relationship with China despite international sanctions against North Korea.

articles.title: Uk Driving Test Booking Rules: UK tightens driving test booking rules after thousands miss appointments | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) is implementing significant changes to its driving test system in response to widespread no-shows, booking abuse, and lengthy waiting times. The latest reforms, effective June 9th, restrict learners' ability to move booked tests and limit the number of changes allowed per booking. These measures aim to ensure fairer access to test slots and reduce the exploitation of the system by third parties. While experts remain divided on whether these restrictions alone can fully address the driving test backlog, the DVSA urges learners to book only when ready and avoid unnecessary changes.

articles.title: ‘They were laughing’: Israel’s use of rape and sexual abuse in prisons | Investigation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Former Palestinian prisoners have detailed accounts of systematic rape and sexual violence by Israeli soldiers, including the use of dogs, during their detention.  The UN has documented evidence of this widespread abuse since October 7, 2023, with reports from organizations like B’Tselem and Physicians for Human Rights Israel. Despite these allegations, Israel has not faced legal censure or sanctions for its actions in Gaza. The international community has condemned the violence and called for accountability, but attempts to investigate have been blocked by Israel.  The UN rapporteur on the occupied territories, Francesca Albanese, stated that the intention behind this abuse is to destroy the victims' sense of self-worth.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Systematic rape and sexual abuse are grave human rights violations.

articles.title: ACB raids nine locations linked to Telangana R&B Engineer-in-Chief in disproportionate assets case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) conducted simultaneous searches at nine locations linked to Roads and Buildings (R&B) Engineer-in-Chief J. Mohan Naik, following a disproportionate assets case against him. The raids targeted Naik's residence in Madhapur and eight other premises associated with him and his relatives.  The ACB is examining documents, financial records, and property papers recovered during the searches to determine if Naik's assets are proportionate to his known income sources.

articles.title: ICC suspends top prosecutor after investigation into misconduct
articles.rephrased_article: The International Criminal Court (ICC) chief prosecutor, Karim Khan, has been suspended while an investigation into misconduct allegations continues. The decision was made by a group within the ICC's management oversight body and referred to the court's 125 member states for a vote on his future.  Khan has denied all allegations of sexual misconduct, with his lawyers calling the decision "unlawful" and "unsupported by evidence." A two-thirds majority would be required to uphold any finding, followed by a separate vote on whether Khan should be removed from office.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: What time can fans in Europe, Middle East and Africa watch? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA has announced the kickoff times for the 2026 World Cup, which will be held across the United States, Mexico and Canada.  Fans in Europe will experience late-night or early morning matches during the first two and a half weeks of the tournament, with some games starting as early as midnight. The semifinals and final are scheduled for 8pm BST/9pm CEST. Qatar viewers will see most matches between 10pm and 7am local time, while fans in the Middle East will experience matches between 10pm and 7am local time.  The first time a record number of African teams will be at the World Cup with games scheduled between 8pm and 5am for North Africa, South Africa, Senegal, and Ghana.

articles.title: MSCI confirms early index inclusion rules ahead of SpaceX IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, is expected to join the MSCI indexes, potentially attracting trillions of dollars in assets from passively managed funds. The rocket maker's $75 billion fundraising and $1.75 trillion valuation have met the size and free-float thresholds for early inclusion.  However, S&P Global has excluded SpaceX from its S&P 500 index due to its lack of profitability. Trading on Nasdaq is scheduled to begin June 12th, with MSCI's decision expected within ten trading days.
